rows.key_quote: Lennar delivered 20,840 homes within its 20,500-21,500 guidance range but new orders of 20,879 fell below the 21,000-22,000 range, down from 23,000 a year ago, as interest rates rose to ~7% and consumer confidence weakened. Gross margin improved sequentially to 15.8% from 15.6% and sales incentives fell to 12%, but SG&A came in at 9.2% above the 8.7%-9% expected range, producing EPS of $1.19 GAAP / $1.23 adjusted on net margin of 6.6%. Q4 guidance calls for 19,500-20,500 new orders, 22,000-23,000 deliveries, 15.5%-16% gross margin, and EPS of $1.30-$1.65. Management flagged a rising land cost basis (up ~6% per homesite) and lengthening land-bank durations as a persistent gross margin headwind, alongside building labor pressure and heavier resale competition in Texas and Florida.

Upexi's fiscal Q4/FY2026 results were dominated by digital asset losses: net loss for the year was $246.1 million, or $3.87 per share, versus a $13.7 million loss ($1.73) in FY2025, driven by $195.1 million of unrealized and $11.7 million of realized digital asset losses and $21.9 million in stock-based compensation. Total stockholders' equity swung to negative $53.8 million from positive $90.1 million a year earlier, while the Treasury held roughly 2.34 million Solana tokens at a $360.3 million cost basis versus $165.3 million in reported Solana value, generating approximately $17.4 million of annualized digital asset (staking) revenue. Management did not provide explicit forward financial guidance beyond stating that cost cuts (headcount from 59 to 10, outsourced operations) should let staking revenue cover ongoing cash expenses beginning in the September 30 quarter, and it highlighted balance-sheet actions including roughly $20 million of debt extinguished, a credit facility refinance to 7.5% from 11.5%, and a $2.8 million share repurchase.

The first half 2026 update was a business and pipeline progress report rather than a quarter with reported revenue or EPS figures. Key events: the Sobi lacutamab partnership closed with a $75 million upfront, the TELLOMAK-3 phase III was initiated with first patient targeted Q1 2027 and an accelerated-approval filing planned H2 2027, and a EUR 30 million equity financing closed. IPH4502 completed phase I dose escalation with objective responses in post-enfortumab vedotin urothelial, NSCLC, and head/neck cancer, with data due at EORTC-NCI-AACR on November 18, 2026; PACIFIC-9 monalizumab phase III enrollment is complete with readout still expected in H2 2026. Cash was EUR 21.4 million as of June 30, 2026, excluding the Sobi and equity proceeds, which are expected to extend the runway through the end of Q1 2028.

LuxExperience delivered on FY2026 guidance with GMV growth of +2.9% constant currency and a positive group-adjusted EBITDA margin of +0.4%. Q4 net sales grew +7.6% (the strongest quarter of the year) with a +2.1% adjusted EBITDA margin, the third consecutive positive quarter; all three segments grew, with Mytheresa +10.2% and a 6.6% adjusted EBITDA margin, NAP/MRP +5.6% and its first positive adjusted EBITDA at 2.7%, and YOOX +6.6% with losses nearly halved to -10.5%. FY2027 guidance is for mid-to-high single-digit group net sales growth and a 2%-3% adjusted EBITDA margin, with segment-level indications and a stated path to 7%-9% medium-term. Management also noted a EUR 442 million cash balance, no bank debt, an ADS buyback authorization, and an expected EUR 150-250 million remaining transformation cash burn.

Evolution Petroleum reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $24.2 million (up 20% sequentially, 15% YoY), net income of $4.6 million or $0.13 per diluted share, and adjusted EBITDA of $6.5 million that more than doubled from $3.1 million in fiscal Q3 but declined from $8.6 million a year ago. Production averaged 6,901 BOE per day, up 3% sequentially but down 4% year-over-year, with adjusted net loss narrowing to $0.6 million from $2.9 million sequentially while remaining below the prior-year adjusted net income of $1.1 million. Full-year production was essentially flat at 7,077 BOE per day versus 7,074, proved reserves were roughly unchanged at 27.2 million barrels of oil equivalent, and the board maintained the quarterly dividend at $0.12 per share for a 52nd consecutive payment. Management gave no production or LOE guidance and set fiscal 2027 CapEx at $4 million-$6 million, excluding potential Chaveroo drilling, while highlighting a post-quarter ~$16 million Permian Midland mineral acquisition adding ~3,420 net royalty acres and over 200 BOE per day.

Q4 revenue was $582,000, bringing FY2026 total to $4.5 million, near the high end of the prior range but roughly flat versus $4.7 million in FY2025. GAAP net loss widened to $4.0 million ($0.22/share) in Q4 and $9.2 million ($0.52/share) for the year, with FY adjusted EBITDA swinging to negative $5.2 million from positive $186,000 in FY2025. Management did not provide formal FY2027 revenue guidance, citing a handful of contracts that could swing the range, but disclosed ~$2.3 million of booked government revenue plus potential for ~$2 million more, and guided FY2027 capex to $10-$12 million for two MOCVD reactors. The main change is a strategic pivot from government R&D revenue toward commercial AI datacom NRE programs, alongside a CHIPS R&D letter of intent for up to $30 million likely to be structured as an equity investment rather than revenue.

Trip.com reported Q2 FY2026 total net revenue of RMB 15.7 billion, up 6% year-over-year, with accommodation revenue up 6% to RMB 6.6 billion (8% ex-contra-revenue item) and transportation ticketing revenue down 1% to RMB 5.4 billion on softer demand, elevated fuel prices, and compliance-related operational adjustments. Adjusted EBITDA fell to RMB 4.6 billion from RMB 4.9 billion a year earlier, while non-GAAP diluted EPS rose to RMB 7.27 from RMB 7.20. The quarter included a one-time RMB 5.18 billion expense and RMB 122 million contra-revenue related to the SAMR anti-monopoly penalty, and management guided to near-term volatility in domestic performance as partners transition to a new operating model. International OTA revenue grew over 50% year-over-year, with inbound travel up high double digits, but no explicit quantitative guidance for Q3 was provided.

Vera Bradley reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $71.6 million, up 1.1% YoY, with Direct segment revenue up 8% to $65.4 million and comps up 9.2%, while Indirect revenue fell 39% to $6.3 million on strategic marketplace shifts and reduced liquidation. Gross margin expanded to 59.8% from 49.9%, though roughly 980 bps of the increase came from $8 million in tariff refunds; underlying gross margin improved more than 40 bps. Net income swung to $3.3 million, or $0.11 per diluted share, from a $0.5 million loss, and inventory fell 28.4% YoY. Management reiterated full-year guidance for sales of $255-$270 million and at least 50% operating profit improvement, with the Direct business momentum and margin discipline offsetting Indirect weakness.

Forgent Power Solutions reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $462 million, up 94% year over year and 22% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $113 million (up 163%) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 24.4%, up 200 basis points sequentially and 640 basis points year over year. Full-year revenue rose 89% to $1.42 billion and adjusted EBITDA rose 91% to $323 million, exceeding both the IPO forecast and the guidance raised in May. Management issued FY2027 guidance for revenue of $2.4–2.6 billion (76% growth at the midpoint), adjusted EBITDA of $575–625 million, and adjusted EPS of $1.26–1.40. Q4 bookings reached a record $1.5 billion and backlog grew to $3 billion, up 256% year over year, with Powertrain Solutions representing approximately 40% of backlog.

High Tide reported Q3 FY2026 record revenue of CAD 198.8 million, up 33% year-over-year (fastest growth in 13 quarters) and 11% sequentially, with record adjusted EBITDA of CAD 16.2 million (up 52% YoY), record operating income of CAD 8.7 million (up 133% YoY), and record net income of CAD 12.7 million (adjusted net income CAD 2.2 million, up 157% YoY). Gross margin held at 27% consolidated, and salaries/wages (11.4% of revenue) and G&A (3.9% of revenue) hit multi-quarter lows. Remexian sold 10.2 tons in Germany, up 35% sequentially, generating CAD 38.2 million revenue and 12% adjusted EBITDA margin. Guidance was issued one business day after quarter-end with the low end exceeding the most aggressive analyst estimates, and results came in near the high end; no formal raised guidance was quantified for the forward quarter, though management reiterated confidence in reaching a CAD 1 billion revenue run rate and noted same-store sales turned positive in June and July.

First half 2026 revenue rose 131% to $11.2 million from $4.8 million, driven by VaultIC demand, PKI/digital identity expansion, initial Quantix Edge revenue and roughly $2.5 million from six months of IC'Alps consolidation; gross profit rose 233% to $5.4 million with gross margin expanding to approximately 48%. However, operating loss widened to $32.2 million from $21.2 million, net loss widened to $27.8 million from $20 million, and EBITDA loss grew to $29.5 million from $20.9 million, reflecting R&D of $8.7 million (versus $4.7 million) and G&A of $23.1 million (versus $13.8 million). Management reaffirmed (did not raise) full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $27 million-$36 million, about 50%-100% growth over 2025's $18.3 million, and reported a $225 million active pipeline with more than $100 million in post-quantum opportunities, though the pipeline was characterized as a management estimate rather than guidance. Liquidity was roughly $486 million in cash, equivalents and restricted cash at June 30, 2026.

51Talk reported Q2 FY2026 gross billings of $39.3 million, up 38.1% YoY and above the high end of June guidance, with net revenues of $32.4 million up 58.8% YoY and gross margin of 73.9%. Operating loss narrowed to $2.1 million from $3.2 million, and net loss attributable to ordinary shareholders was $3.1 million, or GAAP EPS of negative $0.51 and non-GAAP negative $0.43 per ADS. Q3 FY2026 gross billings guidance is $41-43 million, and management described prioritizing more efficient investment toward profitability while noting the prior exceptionally strong Q3 2025 base. Sales and marketing expense rose 48.8% to $19.3 million and product development rose 96.6% to $2.4 million, offsetting much of the top-line improvement.

Dave & Buster's reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $544.1M (down from $557.4M) and a GAAP net loss of $12.5M, or $0.36 per diluted share, versus prior-year net income of $11.4M, or $0.32 per share. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $98.9M (18.2% margin) from $129.7M (23.3% margin), with same-store sales down 2.9% though improving sequentially from down 5.4% in Q1 and down 1.6% in July. Management declined to provide explicit quantitative guidance, saying only it expects same-store sales, revenue and EBITDA to grow in the near term; the only firm forward figures were net CapEx under $200M for FY2026 and potentially $150M or less in FY2027, along with at least $15M in identified cost savings targeted to double. The key change versus the prior quarter is the sequential comp improvement and positive F&B (up 7.6%, fifth straight quarter of growth) offset by a wider EBITDA decline and a swing to a net loss.

Kestra Medical reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $31 million, up 16% YoY (60% growth off a favorable comp, per CFO), with gross margin up over 10 points YoY to 56.5% and 175 bps sequentially, the 11th consecutive quarter of sequential margin expansion. Management raised FY2027 revenue guidance to $141 million (48% growth) from a prior $137 million, and lifted its long-term gross margin target to the mid-70% range from 70%. GAAP net loss widened to $44.1 million from $25.8 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $24 million from $19.4 million a year earlier, on higher commercial and late-stage R&D investment. Q1 cash burn was $32.3 million, with $245 million in cash and investments plus roughly $320 million total liquidity after a new $200 million term loan.

Hain reported Q4 FY2026 organic net sales decline of 2% year-over-year, with North America returning to 2% growth offset by a 4% decline in International. Adjusted gross margin rose 230 bps to 22.7%, adjusted EBITDA fell to $19 million (7.1% margin, up 160 bps), and adjusted net loss widened to $0.05 per diluted share from $0.02. The company announced the sale of its international business to Aurelius for $323 million in cash and provided no traditional fiscal 2027 guidance, citing pending lender amendment discussions and strategic review; it expects pro forma gross margin of 30%+ and low double-digit adjusted EBITDA margin post-close.

American Battery Technology Company reported FY2026 revenue of $21.7 million, up over 400% year-over-year, with cost of goods sold rising only about 67%, producing a first-ever adjusted gross profit of approximately $1.7 million versus a $6.2 million loss the prior year. The company ended the year with $49.5 million in cash, total assets of about $133 million, and no outstanding long-term debt. Management cited operational efficiencies, improved pricing, and grid-scale battery storage demand, while noting that a U.S. Department of Commerce directive banning black mass exports has left that product stored on-site pending an unresolved exception request. Formal annual guidance figures were not provided in the transcript.

RF Industries reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $24.0 million, up 21% year-over-year and 16% sequentially, with GAAP net income of $1.4 million ($0.12 diluted EPS) and non-GAAP net income of $2.2 million ($0.19 diluted EPS) versus $0.04 GAAP and $0.10 non-GAAP a year ago. Gross margin expanded 160 bps to 35.6%, operating income rose to $1.8 million (7.3% margin) from $720,000, and adjusted EBITDA grew 71% to $2.7 million (11.1% of sales), above the 10% long-term target. Management guided Q4 sales to be roughly the same or above Q3, and Q3 bookings of $22.5 million produced a 0.94 book-to-bill with backlog of $18.6 million at quarter-end, rising to $19.8 million as of the call. The quarter's key change was broad-based contribution across custom cabling, interconnect, and integrated systems, with the small cell business beginning to accelerate as anticipated.

Radiant reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $261.4 million, up 18.5% YoY, with net income of $7.517 million or $0.15 diluted (up 53.1%), adjusted net income up 34.5%, and adjusted EBITDA of $10.362 million, up 31.6% with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 240 basis points. Full-year FY2026 revenue was $934.4 million but adjusted EBITDA fell 5.4% to $36.684 million and adjusted net income dropped 18.4% to $25.253 million. No formal FY2027 numeric guidance was issued; management said organic growth was about 8% in Q4 and described improving domestic truckload/intermodal trends (only one month reflected in results) plus a new independent agent program at Radiant Road & Rail launching in Q1 FY2027. The quarter's airfreight strength was partly attributed to disaster relief work following Western Pacific typhoons, and the balance sheet carries no net debt after an amended $200 million credit facility extended to 2031.

CoinShares reported H1 2026 GAAP revenue of $51.4 million, down from $80 million a year earlier, as AUM fell to $5.5 billion from $7.4 billion at December 2025 under a sharp digital asset drawdown (Bitcoin ~-32%, Ethereum ~-48%). Segment EBITDA fell to $21.6 million ($26.5 million adjusted for ~$4.9 million of non-recurring listing/US GAAP costs) versus $59 million a year ago, and the period swung to a $5.1 million operating loss, driven by a $34.7 million unfavorable XBT Pricing Differential swing. Flows were positive at ~$28 million, with CoinShares Physical drawing ~$156 million of net inflows, and AUM had recovered to ~$6.9 billion by August 31, aided by ~$74 million of net inflows post-period. The board is seeking shareholder approval at the AGM for a multi-year buyback authority of up to 25% of shares outstanding (32.9 million shares); no forward financial guidance was given.

Kroger reported Q2 identical sales without fuel of just 0.2% and adjusted EPS of $1.09 (up 5% YoY), with a 265 bp sales drag from IRA/GLP-1 pharmacy changes (~140 bp), brand-to-generic shift (~60 bp), Cyclospora (~35 bp), and egg deflation (~30 bp). FIFO gross margin expanded 13 bp despite the soft top line, aided by e-commerce profitability, retail media (up 24%), pharmacy mix, tariff refunds, and sourcing, partly offset by higher shrink and transportation costs. Management lowered full-year identical sales without fuel guidance to 0.2%-0.8% from 1%-2% but maintained adjusted FIFO operating profit guidance of $5.0-$5.2B and adjusted EPS of $5.10-$5.30, citing cost savings and share repurchases. Adjusted FIFO operating profit was $1.1B and net debt to adjusted EBITDA stood at 1.91x.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was RMB 266.1 million, up 9.9% year-over-year and 2.7% quarter-over-quarter, but total GAAP operating loss widened to RMB 73.6 million from RMB 11.1 million a year earlier (non-GAAP operating loss RMB 25.6 million vs RMB 2.1 million). Advertising agency services revenue fell 70.0% year-over-year to RMB 22.0 million on changed review policies at a major global ad platform, while cloud and AI infrastructure revenue rose 83.1% year-over-year to RMB 59.1 million and robotics and others rose 72.5% to RMB 54.5 million. Management guided to 2026 cloud/AI-infrastructure gross billings above RMB 2 billion (+>100% YoY) and related revenue above RMB 200 million (+>50% YoY), and did not provide formal total-company profit guidance. Internet services adjusted operating margin expanded to 19.4% from 14.1% a year ago.

Adobe reported Q3 FY2026 record revenue of $6.76B, up 13% YoY (12% constant currency), with GAAP EPS of $4.62 (up 11%) and non-GAAP EPS of $6.13 (up 15%). Total ending ARR grew 11.2% to $27.5B, but net new ARR declined 36-37% YoY and RPO grew only 8% YoY, the first single-digit RPO growth since early FY2023. Q4 revenue guidance of $6.8B-$6.85B is a modest sequential uptick, and full-year revenue and EPS targets were raised, partly offset by FX headwinds. Adobe also announced CEO succession (Anil Chakravarthy effective Dec 1) and an agreement to acquire Topaz Labs expected to close in Q4.

Descartes reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $201.1 million, up 12% YoY, with record adjusted EBITDA of $94.4 million (46.9% margin, up 18%) and record net income up 32% to $50 million; GAAP EPS was $1.13 for the first half. Organic services growth was 'just north of 9%', consistent with Q1, and professional services revenue declined slightly to $12.4 million. Management did not raise full-year guidance but pointed to an ongoing Q3 baseline adjusted EBITDA margin of ~38%, below its historical 40–45% target range, due to two recent acquisitions (Tai, Extensiv) with lower initial margins and limited operating history. The quarter was a solid beat on revenue and profitability versus prior-year levels, but no explicit guidance raise was provided.

Yuanbao reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of RMB 1.39 billion, up 30.1% year-over-year, with net income of RMB 413.2 million (up 35.6%) and a 29.7% net margin; non-GAAP adjusted net income was RMB 431.2 million (up 32.6%) at a 31% margin. Growth was driven by insurance distribution revenue of RMB 457.4 million (+30.4%), system services revenue of RMB 881.9 million (+22.8%), plus RMB 52.8 million from a newly launched advertising service. Cash and investments totaled RMB 5.16 billion, up 50.9% year-over-year, and operating cash flow was RMB 419.1 million. Management did not provide explicit numeric guidance; commentary was qualitative, citing stable customer acquisition ROI, a growing rather than reduced dividend, and continued AI/R&D investment, while specific metrics such as advertising margins, policy counts, and average ticket size were withheld.

Copart reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 2.4% year-over-year, but net income fell 17.4% to $327.4 million, or $0.35 per diluted share, down 14.6%. Gross margin contracted to 41.8% as gross profit declined 5.5%, and global sold units fell 2.9% with U.S. units down 5.7% and U.S. insurance units down 7.5%. International was a bright spot, with revenue up 11.7% and units up 10%. Separately, Copart announced an all-cash acquisition of ACV, expected to close by the end of the calendar year and be accretive in FY2028. Management did not provide specific earnings or margin guidance, and noted plans to reduce operating cost per car after a 12.7% increase.

IBEX reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $164.3 million, up 12% YoY and the sixth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with full-year revenue up 15.4% to $644.1 million. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $20.2 million (12.3% of revenue) from $20.5 million (13.9%) on training costs for new client wins, nearshore-to-offshore work transfers, and higher fuel prices, while adjusted EPS slipped to $0.85 from $0.87 and GAAP EPS dropped to $0.59. Management guided FY2027 revenue to $700-715 million (9-11% growth) and Adjusted EBITDA to $90-94 million, with Q1 revenue of $168-170 million and said EBITDA margins should resume expanding. Health tech grew 42% in Q4 and surpassed the $100 million full-year target at $114 million, and the company cited accelerating new-logo wins (nine in Q4, 17 for the year) and AI agent deployments across five verticals.

LightPath reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $21.2 million, up 73% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 39.4% from 22%. Adjusted EBITDA swung to a $2.1 million profit from a $2.0 million loss, marking the fourth consecutive positive quarter. Full-year revenue grew 93% to $71.7 million, backlog rose 197% to $110.9 million, and cash ended at $93.2 million with no debt. Management guided to higher CapEx in FY2027 to expand capacity, and noted two large post-quarter orders totaling $24 million.

Legacy Q4 net sales rose 21.5% to $96.6 million with legacy adjusted EBITDA up 95.6% to $18.6 million and legacy gross margin expanding about 690 bps to 30%; including a six-week contribution from the acquired Chaparral and Robalo brands, consolidated net sales were $129.9 million (up 63.4%) and adjusted EBITDA $20.5 million (up 114.9%). Full-year legacy net sales were $315.6 million (up 11%) with adjusted EBITDA of $43.8 million (up 79.6%), above the increased guidance given last quarter. GAAP results swung to a $7 million loss ($0.35 per diluted share) on a $10.1 million non-cash Crest intangible impairment, acquisition purchase accounting and transaction costs. Guidance for the six-month July-December 2026 transition period is net sales of $287-291 million, adjusted EBITDA of $29-32 million and adjusted EPS of $0.66-0.76, with retail demand assumed down 5%-10% and Chaparral/Robalo production held near Q4 exit rates after a temporary pause of the Chaparral Surf Series.

Culp reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $54.0 million versus $50.7 million a year ago, with bedding sales up 13.2% to $31.8 million and upholstery roughly flat at $22.2 million. GAAP gross margin jumped to 28.5% from 14.3%, aided by roughly $7 million in one-time IEEPA tariff recoveries; excluding those recoveries gross margin was 15.6% (about 17% gross profit growth) and non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $271,000 from $1.9 million. Net income was $6.0 million, or $0.47 per diluted share, versus a net loss of $0.02 per share, and net debt fell roughly 70% to $3.1 million. Management provided limited guidance, expecting consistent sequential sales, year-over-year growth, break-even operating income, and accelerating adjusted EBITDA in Q2.

FEIM reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $23.5 million, up 70% year-over-year and 52% sequentially, with net income of $4.2 million or $0.41 per share versus $634,000 or $0.07 a year earlier. Gross margin was 45.8% and operating margin 22%, versus 50% and 30% three-year minimum targets set in July, and backlog reached a record $129 million, up 82% year-over-year and 16% sequentially. Management said the quarter increases confidence in meeting or exceeding the $150 million-plus fiscal 2029 revenue target, possibly sooner and potentially a substantially larger number, and completed a roughly $73 million secondary offering to fund capacity expansion. Book-to-bill was approximately 1.76 to 1, with about 65% of backlog scheduled within 12 months.

Oracle reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of a record $19.3 billion, up 30% year-over-year, with cloud infrastructure revenue of $7.4 billion up 121% and non-GAAP EPS of $1.92 up 30%. Non-GAAP operating income rose 31% to $8.2 billion with operating margin roughly flat at 42%, while gross margin declined as expected on data center ramp and mix. RPO increased $26 billion from Q4, and full-year guidance was raised to at least $90 billion in total revenue (+34%) and $8.10 in non-GAAP EPS, versus prior guidance. CapEx for the full year is still anticipated at $90-95 billion with negative free cash flow of $5 billion in Q1.

Designer Brands reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $730.6 million, down about 1% YoY, with comps down 2.4% and retail comps down 2.6%, driven by a sandals shortfall that accounted for roughly 200 bps of the retail decline, partially offset by an 18% increase in brand portfolio sales. Adjusted EPS was $0.34 versus $0.33 last year, and adjusted operating income rose to $39.4 million with a 140 bp margin improvement, aided by $20.2 million of tariff refunds. Management raised full-year sales guidance to flat to up 1% from a prior -1% to +1%, and increased adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $0.47-$0.52 from $0.28-$0.38. The company also noted that retail trends returned to slightly positive quarter to date, with athletic demand improving 400 bps in August and back-to-school performing ahead of expectations.

Net sales rose only 0.4% to $161.2 million with omni-channel comps down 1.9%, though gross margin jumped 1,200 bps to 68.4% and EPS swung to $0.51 from -$0.45, both driven largely by a $21 million IEEPA tariff refund ($0.86 per share benefit). Adjusted EBITDA, excluding the refund, was a $1.3 million loss versus $0.8 million income a year earlier. Management lowered its Q3 and full-year outlook, citing later-than-planned timing of major new product launches and a mid-event Labor Day read, and said its pricing/promotional changes have not yet returned the under-$6,000 segment to growth.

Alliance Entertainment reported FY2026 revenue up 8% to $1.15 billion, gross margin up 80 bps to 13.3%, adjusted EBITDA up 14% to $41.5 million, and adjusted diluted EPS up 24% to $0.46. However, GAAP operating income fell to $27.2 million from $30.1 million and net income declined to $13.1 million from $15.1 million, largely due to a $7.8 million non-cash write-off of a Tastemakers vendor rebate receivable. Operating cash flow swung to a $1.7 million use from $26.8 million generated, as working capital (inventory and receivables) grew faster than revenue, and SG&A rose 18% to $66 million. Management provided no formal guidance for FY2027, but described robust demand, full-year Amazon MGM contribution, collectibles growth, and a major GTA VI holiday release as drivers.

Q2 net sales rose 1.1% to $4.9B and total revenue rose 1.2% to $5.1B, with comps up 2.7% (go-forward +2.8%); adjusted EPS of $0.63 (including a ~$0.23 net tariff refund benefit) compared to $0.35 last year, and adjusted EPS ex-refunds was up 14% and above the high end of guidance. Gross margin expanded to 41.5% from 39.7%, though underlying gross margin was up only ~10 bps, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $457M (9.0% of revenue) from $373M (7.5%). Full-year guidance was raised to net sales of $21.675-21.825B and adjusted EPS of $2.15-$2.35 (from the prior $1.90-$2.10 start to the year), with Q3 comps guided to -0.5% to +0.5% and an adjusted EPS loss of $0.19-$0.23. Second-half sales expectations were kept in line with the prior outlook despite the Q2 beat, with tariff/fuel headwind guidance improved to 5-15 bps from 20-30 bps.

RH reported Q2 GAAP net revenues of $922.2 million, above the high end of guidance and up 2.6% YoY (~4.2 points acceleration over Q1). Adjusted EBITDA margin of 13.4% also exceeded the high end of guidance, with $72.3 million of cash generated and a $55.1 million tariff benefit recognized. Management raised the FY2026 outlook to 5.5%-7% revenue growth and a 15%-16.2% adjusted EBITDA margin, with a significant Q4 revenue guide of 16.1%-21.2% tied to the November launch of the RH Estates collection. The offset is a noted ~$50 million of unplanned supply chain cost increases from the oil spike, mitigated by an additional $13.9 million tariff benefit, and a still-murky housing/Europe macro backdrop.

Q2 FY2026 net sales fell 7.2% to $284.3M with comps down 7.1%, gross margin compressed 690 bps to 31.9%, and EPS dropped to $0.23 from $0.70. Management lowered full-year guidance to net sales of $1.1B-$1.111B (down 2%-3%), adjusted EPS of $0.75-$0.90, and gross margin of ~32.5%-32.7% (390-410 bps of compression), explicitly not assuming any promotional or margin improvement. The key change versus the prior quarter was the guidance cut, partly offset by an improved August comp of -2.7% (from -7.1% in Q2) driven by localized athletic assortments, though Shoe Station continued down mid-high single digits.

Vince reported Q2 fiscal 2026 net sales of $81.8 million, up 11.7% year-over-year, with DTC up 13.7% and wholesale up 10.4%. GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.80 from $0.93, but adjusted EPS rose to $1.02 from $0.38 and adjusted EBITDA reached $18 million versus $6.7 million excluding the prior-year ERC benefit; reported results included $10.4 million of tariff refunds, and excluding those, gross margin fell 290 basis points. Management raised the full-year Vince outlook to approximately 8%-10% net sales growth and 9%-9.5% adjusted EBITDA margin, while guiding Q3 Vince sales to 5%-8% growth. The company also completed the acquisition of OVO, a streetwear brand with nearly $50 million in calendar 2025 net sales, expected to be earnings neutral this year and accretive in fiscal 2027.

Zumiez reported Q2 FY2026 net sales down 2.5% to $209 million with comparable sales down 2.1%, citing U.S. softness (North America comps -2.9%) offset by positive international comps (other international +2.1%). Gross margin contracted 20 bps to 35.3% and the company swung to an operating loss of $1.3 million and a net loss of $0.17 per share versus a $0.06 loss a year ago. Management guided Q3 sales down 5.5%-7% with comps of -5% to -6.5%, and retracted prior full-year operating margin growth guidance of 50-100 bps, now expecting a slight decline while refraining from specific full-year EPS guidance. Results fell short of expectations due to U.S. footwear weakness, and quarter-to-date trends through Labor Day remained soft, prompting a conservative outlook.

Imperial Petroleum reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $87.1 million, up 140% year-over-year and 41.2% sequentially, with net income of $34.8 million (EPS $0.75) versus $12.8 million (EPS $0.36) in Q2 2025; first-half net income of $62.8 million already exceeded full-year 2025's $50 million. Cash and deposits rose to $245.2 million at June 30 (about $260 million currently), with zero debt and six-month operating cash flow of $78 million. The company took delivery of two vessels, sold the Suez Enchanted for a profit above $30 million, and targets a 25-vessel fleet by year-end while noting seven remaining dry dockings in 2026. Guidance was qualitative only, with management citing geopolitical tensions and an undisclosed impact from a dry bulk vessel stranded in the Strait of Hormuz.

Reformation reported its first public quarter with Q2 FY2026 net revenue up 24.1% to $155.2 million, beating the high end of IPO-period estimates, with DTC up 21.2% to $135.3 million, wholesale up 48.7% to $19.9 million, and international up 36.8% to $31.2 million. Gross margin expanded roughly 230 bps to 66.7% on lower tariff rates and higher AUR, driving adjusted EBITDA up 54% to $25.4 million (16.4% margin) and net income to $12.4 million. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is $602-$606 million (18.6%-19.5% growth) with adjusted EBITDA margin of 14%-14.2%, reflecting Q2 outperformance and current Q3 trends; Q3 revenue is expected to exceed Q4. LTM active customers grew 23% to 1.2 million, while DTC net revenue per customer fell 1.4% on outsized new-customer mix.

TEN reported Q2 2026 net income of $139.3 million, or $4.40 per share, versus $26.8 million, or $0.67, a year earlier — a 557% EPS increase — on gross revenues of $298 million versus $193 million. First-half net income reached $228 million ($7.12 per share) from $64.5 million ($1.70), with TCE per ship per day of $43,503 versus $30,754, a 41% increase. Profit-sharing revenue was $71 million in the first half ($30.5 million in Q2) versus $10 million a year earlier, and management guided to a significant second-half increase, with 13 profit-sharing vessels including seven Suezmaxes and two VLCCs. TEN also announced the sale of two 2006-built Suezmaxes for net proceeds of $100 million and said it expects to increase the semi-annual dividend after its November strategy meeting.

Oddity Q2 FY2026 net revenue fell 25% YoY to $181 million, at the favorable end of guidance for a 25-30% decline, with adjusted EBITDA of $13 million beating the $8-10 million outlook and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.20. Gross margin compressed ~360 bps to 68.7% and first orders fell ~40% amid an ongoing ad-account algorithm dislocation at IL MAKIAGE, partly offset by SpoiledChild tracking to ~$350 million in 2026 revenue and METHODIQ's early ramp. Q3 revenue is guided to decline ~5% YoY with adjusted EBITDA of $18-20 million, while FY2026 revenue is guided down ~19% with EBITDA of $30-32 million. The company repurchased 5.6 million shares for $80 million in the quarter and repurchased $50 million face value of its June 2030 exchangeable notes for $35 million.

Jersey Mike's reported Q2 FY2026 same-store sales growth of 2.3%, accelerating from 1.7% in Q1, with system-wide sales up 10% to ~$1.21 billion and total revenues up 10% to $208 million; adjusted EBITDA rose 7% to $114 million, pressured by a $10 million advertising expense timing swing that reduced EBITDA growth by ~11 points (ex-timing, EBITDA would have grown 18%). The company guided full-year 2026 same-store sales to 2.5%-3% (including 3%-4% in Q3), net unit growth of at least 8%, and adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 20% (at least 13% in Q3). Key changes included the completion of a $300 million IPO used to repay debt, reducing leverage to ~4.4x, and the ongoing shift to digital marketing representing over 20% of spend, with digital mix reaching 43% of sales.

Q3 FY2026 total net revenue fell to $43.8 million from $47.5 million a year ago, with agribusiness revenue down to $42.2 million, and GAAP net loss widened to $3.0 million or $0.17 per diluted share; adjusted EPS was $0.02 versus $(0.02) prior year and adjusted EBITDA rose to $3.9 million from $3.0 million. Lemon volume guidance was trimmed to 4.0-4.25 million cartons on Argentine import oversupply, while avocado volume guidance was raised for a second time to 7.0-7.25 million pounds for FY2026 with a 30%-plus increase expected in FY2027. Management pointed to a Q4 water-rights monetization, the $15 million Windfall Farms sale closing September 14, 2026, and $10 million of targeted SG&A savings, reiterating positive Q4 adjusted EBITDA.

17EdTech reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 90.1 million, up 254.6% year-over-year from RMB 25.4 million, with gross margin expanding 11.7 percentage points to 69.2% from 57.5% and up from 61.9% in Q1. The company posted its first quarterly GAAP net profit of RMB 1.1 million and adjusted non-GAAP net income of RMB 4.7 million, versus a GAAP net loss of RMB 26.0 million a year ago, while operating loss narrowed to RMB 0.6 million from RMB 28.5 million. Cash rose to RMB 456.9 million from RMB 407.0 million at year-end 2025, and the board authorized a new up-to-$10 million share repurchase program. Management cited expansion of the Yiqi Aixue consumer AI membership and district/school subscription projects, and pointed to the Minhang District shift from SaaS toward agentic services, but declined to provide explicit forward revenue or margin guidance and cautioned against extrapolating any single quarter.

Cooper reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $1.066 billion, up ~1% reported and organic, with non-GAAP EPS up 4% to $1.15 and record quarterly free cash flow of $273 million. CooperVision revenue was $717 million, essentially flat, due to a proactive U.S. channel inventory reduction that will also pressure Q4; CooperSurgical grew 3% organically with fertility up 5%. Q4 guidance implies consolidated organic growth of 0%-2% and EPS of $1.05-$1.09, below the prior Q3 run rate, while the company also announced a $307 million tax benefit and a $1 billion increase to its buyback authorization. The strategic review concluded with the board deciding to retain CooperSurgical rather than watch.

Wealthfront reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $91.9 million, up just 1% year-over-year, with cash management revenue down 10% to $61.8 million on a lower 55 bps cash fee rate. Adjusted EBITDA fell 15% year-over-year to $38.1 million (41% margin, down 8 points), and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.10. Offsetting this were Investment Advisory strength — assets up 30% to $54.1 billion, revenue up 31% to $28.8 million — and total platform assets crossing $100 billion in August at $100.9 billion. Management gave no formal guidance, noting near-term Home Lending investment headwinds to margins but reiterating long-term 40%+ EBITDA margin potential.

Signet reported Q2 revenue of $1.5 billion with same-store sales up 2.2%, adjusted EPS up 36% to a level driving adjusted operating income up 25% to $107 million and adjusted gross margin rate up 70 bps. Management raised full-year guidance for the second time, lifting the low end of same-store sales guidance by 75 bps to flat to up 2.5% and increasing adjusted operating income and EPS guidance by over 10%, with roughly two-thirds of the EPS raise from the new Bread Financial credit agreement, tariff refunds, and buybacks and one-third from core performance. The company signed an early seven-year renewal with Bread Financial expected to generate over $1 billion in incremental non-comp revenue and operating income through 2035, including $200-$250 million over the next 36 months and approximately $80 million of cash in Q3. Q3 guidance calls for same-store sales of down 1% to up 2% and adjusted operating income of $31-$48 million, with the smallest quarter of the year facing higher incentive compensation.

SailPoint reported Q2 FY2027 total ARR of $1.231 billion, up 25% YoY and $11 million above the midpoint of guidance, with SaaS ARR up 36% to $847 million and net new SaaS ARR up 34% to $66 million (97% of total net new ARR). Total revenue rose 17% YoY to $309 million, adjusted operating margin was 20.3%, free cash flow was $37 million, and RPO accelerated to 30% growth at $1.9 billion. Management raised full-year FY2027 ARR guidance by $11 million to $1.38 billion and reiterated FY2029 targets of at least $2.1 billion ARR and $800 million AI-driven ARR. AI-driven ARR crossed $70 million, AI-driven pipeline more than doubled since Investor Day to over $200 million, and customers adopting AI solutions increased annual spend by over 60%, though a higher SaaS mix created roughly a $5 million in-period revenue timing headwind.

Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 24% YoY to $59.6 million, with net income attributable to common stock of $2.5 million, or $0.31 per diluted share, versus $0.9 million and $0.10 a year earlier; results absorbed a $3.9 million uncollectible receivable charge offset by a $1.6 million tax benefit. Gross margin held at ~29%, in line with the prior year's ~30%, while income from operations rose to $4.3 million from $3.2 million; first-half net income fell to $4.3 million from $5.8 million on the write-off. Backlog grew to $142.3 million from $121.6 million at year-end, and the company secured $67.8 million in new orders. Management guided to a strong second half, citing Ohio and Qatar facility ramps (full production by early 2027), Saudi Aramco qualification of a new product line, and a new $90 million JPMorgan credit facility, but gave no explicit numerical guidance.

Q2 FY2027 revenue was $233 million, up 35% year-over-year, with GBV of just over $3 billion, up 45%, and non-GAAP operating margin of 7%, up from 5% a year ago. The company exceeded expectations for both revenue and non-GAAP operating income and raised full-year revenue guidance to $927–$933 million (32% growth at the midpoint) and non-GAAP operating income guidance to $82–$86 million (9% margin). Subscription revenue grew 39% to $21 million, payment volume grew 34% to $1.3 billion, and free cash flow turned positive at $28 million on a trailing 12-month basis versus a $33 million burn a year ago. The acquisition of BoomPop adds meetings and events capability with a very low single-digit revenue impact in FY27 and expected accretion in FY28.

J.Jill reported Q2 net sales of $154.8 million, up 0.5% YoY, with comps up 0.5%; adjusted EPS was $1.24 versus $0.81 last year and adjusted EBITDA excluding tariff refunds and investments was $20.1 million. Reported gross margin was 76.8% (up ~840 bps) including $13.3 million of net tariff refunds, but was roughly flat at 68.3% excluding refunds. Management raised full-year sales guidance to flat to up 2% and adjusted EBITDA to $75-80 million, and guided Q3 sales up 3-5% with comps up 1-3%, while deploying most tariff refunds into second-half marketing and technology investments.

Q2 FY2027 revenue was $46.6 million, up 188% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, exceeding both revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance; platform solutions revenue rose 209% to $22.9 million and cost of revenue fell to 64.0% of revenue from 74.8% a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA improved $3.2 million sequentially to negative $8.3 million, though the quarter included a $4.4 million restructuring charge for acquisition integration. Management raised full-year FY2026 revenue guidance by $5 million to $200 million, guided Q3 revenue to $55 million with adjusted EBITDA narrowing to negative $3.5 million, and reiterated a commitment to adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4 2026 and free cash flow positive in the back half of 2027. Other changes versus prior periods include a completed $23.7 million net follow-on offering, $39.3 million in cash as of July 31, 2026, a one-year extension of the $13.2 million senior secured loan to April 2028, and more than 30 customers now at over $1 million in annual contract value including a first $10 million ACV customer.

Core & Main reported Q2 net sales of approximately $2.1 billion, up 2.5% year over year, with volume, price, and acquisitions each contributing slightly. Adjusted EBITDA rose about 3% to $274 million as Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 10 basis points to 12.8% on roughly flat SG&A of $301 million, and Adjusted Diluted EPS increased 8% to $0.94. Full-year guidance was affirmed at net sales of $7.8-$7.9 billion, Adjusted EBITDA of $950-$980 million, and operating cash flow conversion of 60%-70%, unchanged from prior guidance. Fire protection sales rose 14% (about two-thirds price/steel), treatment plant grew double digits to a mid-single-digit share of sales, data center contribution nearly doubled year over year, while residential lot development fell high single digits and PVC pricing stayed flat with announced increases failing to stick.

Cognyte reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of approximately $109 million, up 12% year over year, with total software revenue up 20.9% to $100.8 million and recurring revenue up 18.4% to $56.2 million. Non-GAAP operating income rose 52.5% to $12.2 million, adjusted EBITDA increased 35.7% to $14.9 million, and non-GAAP EPS nearly doubled to $0.15 from $0.08, while non-GAAP gross margin expanded 154 basis points to 73.7%. The company narrowed full-year revenue guidance around an unchanged ~$448 million midpoint (12% growth) and reiterated FY2027 non-GAAP operating income of ~$66 million, adjusted EBITDA of ~$68 million, and EPS of $0.47, while noting it will not quantify the cash flow impact of a deliberate inventory build. Key changes versus prior periods include a third consecutive decline in total RPO to $470.2 million and a shift in language on full-year operating cash flow from a specific $45 million expectation to 'significantly positive'.

Caleres reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.47 versus $0.35 last year, with sales of $695 million up 5.6% (down 0.8% excluding Stuart Weitzman). Brand portfolio organic sales rose 8.2% and brand portfolio operating margin expanded 740 bps to 10.5%, but Famous Footwear sales fell 6.3% with comps down 5.9% on a late back-to-school and lifestyle athletic weakness. Management raised the low end of full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.50-$1.65 (high end maintained) as Q3 adjusted EPS is guided to $0.62-$0.70, while noting continued Famous softness and promotional pressure in the back half.

Academy reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $1.6 billion, up 3% with comparable sales down 0.4%, as July turned positive but May/June ran down 1% on a comp basis. Gross margin rose roughly 440 bps to 40.4% on tariff refunds, diluted EPS rose 17.3% to $2.17 and adjusted EPS rose 19.1% to $2.31, though the tariff refund contributed only $0.06 to EPS after reinvestment into price, labor, and marketing. Full-year sales guidance was affirmed at 3%-5% growth with comps flat to +2%, gross margin guidance was raised to 35.5%-36.0%, and EPS guidance was raised to $6.05-$6.45 (adjusted $6.50-$6.90) on a lower share count. Management flagged a challenged consumer, with under-$50,000 household traffic down high single digits and footwear down 1%, while e-commerce grew 12.8% and new stores comped mid-single digits.

Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.4 billion rose 8% with comparable sales up 6%, and operating income of $211 million versus $103 million last year included a $161 million net tariff refund benefit; gross margin of 48.7% was up 980 bps, driven 1,300 bps by $179 million of tariff refunds while merchandise margins deleveraged 330 bps. Aerie total sales grew 25% with comps up 19%, while American Eagle total sales rose 1% with comps down 1%. Full-year operating income guidance was trimmed to $540-$550 million from roughly $555 million, driven by American Eagle now guided flat for the back half versus prior low-single-digit positive, plus markdown placeholders; Q3 operating income is guided to $110-$115 million on mid-to-high single-digit comps.

Sunbelt reported record Q1 FY2027 results with total revenue up 11.2% to $3.1 billion and rental revenue up 12.5% to $2.9 billion, citing broad-based growth in General Tool (rental revenue +7.4%) and Specialty (rental revenue +25.3%). Adjusted EPS rose 20.4% to $1.18 while adjusted EBITDA grew 8.7% to $1.3 billion at a 42.2% margin, down from 43.2% due to ancillary revenue mix. The company raised fiscal 2027 guidance for total revenue growth to 6-9%, rental revenue growth to 7-10%, adjusted EBITDA to $4.92-5.12 billion, and increased gross and net rental capital expenditure ranges. Management expressed confidence in sustaining momentum, highlighting accelerating rental rates, tight supply-demand, stable local construction markets, and expectations for flat year-over-year margins with operating profit progression.

Korn Ferry reported Q1 FY2027 consolidated fee revenue up 7% year-over-year to $756 million, its sixth consecutive quarter of growth, with adjusted EBITDA up 7% to $128 million (17.0% margin, flat year-over-year) and adjusted diluted EPS up 9% to $1.43. Estimated remaining fees under existing contracts rose 14% year-over-year to $1.92 billion, and consolidated new business grew 12%. The company closed its combination with AMS last week, adding roughly $650 million in annualized revenue and a backlog of about $3.5 billion combined, and guided Q2 fee revenue to $860-$878 million, adjusted EBITDA margin to 16.8%-17.2%, and adjusted EPS to $1.30-$1.40, including only two months of AMS. Guidance assumptions include incremental AMS intangible amortization, interest expense, and shares issued; no prior-period guidance comparison was provided in the text.

Casey's reported Q1 FY2027 diluted EPS of $7.37, up 28% YoY, on total revenue of $5.68 billion (+24.3%) and EBITDA of $485 million (+17%). Inside same-store sales rose 3.2% with inside gross margin up 30 bps to 42.2%, PF&DB same-store sales up 4.8% at a 59.3% margin, and fuel margin of $0.478/gallon on same-store gallons down 0.3%. Management did not update annual guidance, reiterating its practice of updating on the Q2 call, while noting August trends were within annual ranges and that CEFCO remodel disruption (~25 bps inside, ~50 bps fuel) should inflect favorably around Q4. Key changes versus prior periods: prepared food traffic-led growth with minimal pricing, cheese costs down 9% YoY to $1.93/lb, and elevated operating expense growth (+8%) with same-store opex up 5% ex-credit card fees.

AV reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $480 million with adjusted EBITDA of $53 million (11% of revenue) and adjusted EPS of $0.59, up 84% year-over-year from $0.32. Bookings were $683 million (1.4x book-to-bill) and funded backlog hit a record $1.5 billion, up 37% year-over-year and 23% sequentially, while total funded and unfunded backlog was approximately $2.8 billion. The company reaffirmed full-year FY2027 guidance: revenue of $2.125-$2.225 billion (~10% growth at midpoint), adjusted EBITDA of $305-$325 million, and non-GAAP EPS of $3.02-$3.34, with a 45/55 first-half/second-half revenue split. Segment results were mixed: Autonomous Systems revenue rose 21% to $346 million, but Space, Cyber and Directed Energy revenue fell 21% to $134 million on the SCAR contract termination and discontinued programs, producing a negative $9 million segment adjusted EBITDA.

OCC reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 22% YoY to $24.3 million and net income of $1.9 million, or $0.21 per diluted share, versus $302,000, or $0.04, a year earlier, with gross profit up 43.9% to $9.1 million and gross margin expanding to 37.4% from 31.7%. Backlog and forward load rose to $13.5 million from $13.3 million at April 30, $10.4 million at January 31 and $7.3 million at October 31, and the company said demand is strong across enterprise, data center and specialty markets, including military. Management reaffirmed its prior expectation that the second half of fiscal 2026 would be very strong and said optical fiber shortages and longer lead times for certain raw materials remain the primary impediments to ramping manufacturing, though the company does not provide forward guidance.

Chewy reported Q2 net sales of $3.33 billion, up 7.3% year-over-year (5.7% organic), with adjusted EBITDA of $227 million (6.8% margin) beating guidance of 6.3%-6.4% and adjusted EPS of $0.36. Management narrowed FY2026 organic sales growth to 5.5%-6.3% and raised the low end of adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 6.7%-6.8% from 6.6%-6.8%, but noted essentially all of the Q2 EBITDA beat came from timing-related and discrete items ($10 million tariff/rebate timing plus $5 million gift card/inventory benefits). The consumer backdrop remains pressured with discretionary treats and hardgoods softness, though trends have stabilized, not deteriorated, versus prior assumptions. Free cash flow fell to $90 million from $106 million on timing, and the company repurchased 9.9 million shares for $200 million.

Q2 2026 revenue was $4.2 million, up 37% YoY from $3.0 million, driven mainly by $0.9 million from the consolidated Nanox Health IT business; teleradiology contributed $3 million, AI/software $1 million, and imaging systems/OEM only $0.2 million. GAAP gross margin was -1,051% versus -107%, and a $40.7 million non-cash impairment of AI-solution intangibles drove GAAP net loss to $55.5 million from $14.7 million, while non-GAAP net loss was $11.6 million and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $11.3 million from $10.4 million. Management cited operational frictions (permitting, shielding, construction, workflow integration) for slower-than-expected commercialization, guided to realizing commercial progress 'in the next few months,' announced a Korea restructuring (chip line idled, ~67% Korea headcount cut, ~15% Israel headcount cut, ~$2 million annualized savings from 2027), and raised $8.5 million gross post-quarter via ATM and a registered direct offering, with cash at $31.4 million versus $60 million at year-end 2025.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 26% to $450 million on 38% higher avocado volume (253 million lbs), but GAAP EPS was -$0.08 with adjusted EPS of $0.18 versus $0.26 last year; adjusted EBITDA of $32.4 million exceeded the high end of the $28-$32 million guidance but was roughly flat versus $32.6 million a year ago. Gross margin fell 270 bps to 9.9% and the international farming segment Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $7.6 million from $12.1 million on lower average watching prices. Management reaffirmed its second-half Adjusted EBITDA range of $84-$88 million, implying a Q4 jump to $52-$55 million on the Peru harvest, blueberry seasonality, a full Calavo quarter and initial synergies, and raised its annualized Calavo synergy estimate to more than $30 million from at least $25 million.

InnovAge reported FY2026 revenue of $989.7 million, up 15.9%, with adjusted EBITDA of $94.6 million versus $34.5 million in FY2025 (a ~175% increase) and center-level contribution margin up 500 bps to 23.0%. Q4 revenue rose 4.0% sequentially to $262.0 million and Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $24.3 million, down from $30.5 million in Q3, though net income turned positive at $9.8 million versus a $29.9 million loss in Q3. FY2027 guidance targets revenue of $1.05-$1.085 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $105-$115 million on census growth of 5%-7.5%, implying margin expansion to roughly 10.3% despite a more tempered Medicare rate increase of 1.5%-2.0% and final Medicaid rate outcomes still unresolved in California and Colorado, which represent ~70% of census.

Canaan reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of approximately $32 million, below its prior guidance range of $35-45 million, with product revenue of $14 million, mining revenue of $18 million, 2.5 EH/s of computing power sold, and 243 Bitcoin mined. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $74.9 million, including non-cash inventory write-downs, PP&E impairments, and digital asset fair value losses, while cash rose to $66 million from $43 million at the end of Q1. Management guided Q3 FY2026 revenue to $11-15 million, well below the Q2 level, citing cautious miner procurement, elevated industry inventory, and aggressive competitor pricing; Q2 product revenue declined sharply from $40 million cited in the CEO's remarks referenced as product revenue for the quarter. The company also sold all Ethereum and 54 Bitcoins in late August to fund $5.4 million of ADS repurchases.

ABM reported Q3 FY2026 record revenue of ~$2.3B, up 4.2% YoY (2.1% organic, 2.1% from WGNSTAR), with adjusted EPS up 27% to $1.04 and adjusted EBITDA up 11% to $139.6M. The company raised the midpoint of full-year adjusted EPS to $3.95-$4.10 and raised reported free cash flow guidance to ~$210M from ~$185M, based on $199.6M of YTD FCF versus $42.4M a year ago. Segment margin was 7.7%, up 40 bps sequentially but flat YoY, with B&I down 2.6% as expected and Technical Solutions organic growth at just 2% on ~$15M of client project deferrals that management expects to shift into Q4. Aviation grew 12% but margin fell to 5.6% from 6.8% on airline cost-relief requests tied to higher jet fuel.

EVI reported record fiscal 2026 revenue of approximately $447 million and record gross profit of approximately $141 million, with record gross margin of 31.5% as gross profit grew faster than revenue. The company generated roughly $21 million of operating cash flow and ended June with about $44 million of net debt, essentially unchanged from the prior year. Management disclosed no formal quantitative guidance for fiscal 2027, instead citing a substantial acquisition pipeline, a new consumer garment care division anchored by Sudsies, and continued investment in technology including a CRM. The fourth quarter showed commercial laundry Adjusted EBITDA margin above 10% before corporate expense, but no Q4 revenue, EPS, or prior-period comparisons were given on the call.

Gamehaus reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $24.3 million, down 20.8% year-over-year and at the low end of its $23-26 million outlook, with net income of $0.9 million versus $1.5 million a year ago and an operating loss of $0.8 million (operating margin -3.1% versus +4.6%). Full-year revenue fell 11.4% to $104.7 million while net income was roughly flat at $3.9 million, aided by $2.5 million of other income. Management guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $20-23 million, implying further sequential decline, as it shifts the legacy casual and social casino portfolio to a cash-flow/profitability focus and redirects resources toward generative AI. Offsets included ARPDAU up 11.6% to $0.577, payer conversion of 2.5% versus 2.3%, DTC mix reaching 16.2% with a target above 20% by December 31, 2026, and cash rising to $17.6 million.

Waterdrop reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of CNY 1.448 billion, up 72.8% year-over-year, with insurance revenue of CNY 1.333 billion, up 80.5% YoY and 15.4% QoQ, and operating profit of CNY 111 million, up 14.3% YoY and 39.2% QoQ. Net profit attributable to shareholders was CNY 126-130 million, down 10.3% YoY but up 27.9% QoQ, with the YoY decline attributed to tax-related items and non-recurring gains/losses. Management guided for full-year 2026 revenue growth of more than 40% YoY and operating profit growth of over 10% YoY, and announced a sixth buyback program of up to $50 million over 12 months plus a ~$10.8 million cash dividend. Total costs and expenses rose 80.5% YoY to CNY 1.337 billion, driven by a CNY 450 million increase in third-party traffic marketing spend.

IRSA reported FY2026 net income of ARS 420.9 billion versus ARS 261.9 billion a year earlier, driven largely by a positive ARS 193.7 billion swing in fair value change, and record rental-segment adjusted EBITDA of almost $200 million. Tenant sales fell 8.5% in real terms while mall revenues rose 1.5% on inflation-adjusted fixed rents, occupancy held near 97%, and shopping-mall EBITDA margin slipped to 66% from 67.9% on one-off costs. Management guided to roughly $150 million of FY2027 CapEx excluding new acquisitions, a Net Debt/EBITDA that will rise above the current 1.4x, and a coming dividend proposal, while not giving explicit EBITDA guidance for the development segment.

Braze reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $227 million, up 26% year-over-year and 8% sequentially, with non-GAAP operating income of $22 million (9.7% margin) versus $6 million (3.4%) a year ago. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.19 versus $0.15, and record Q2 free cash flow was $22 million. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance to $229-230 million (~20% growth) and increased full-year revenue and operating income guidance, while gross margin declined to 68.6% from 69.3% on premium messaging and Decisioning Studio costs. The company completed a $50 million accelerated share repurchase and reported large-customer DBNR improving to 112%.

UNFI reported Q4 FY2026 sales of over $7.6 billion (down less than 1% YoY) and full-year sales of approximately $31.2 billion, in line with the updated June outlook. Full-year adjusted EBITDA reached $701 million (up 27%) and adjusted EPS of $2.65 came in above the high end of guidance, while free cash flow of $323 million was the highest ever and net leverage fell to 2.2x from 4x two years ago. For FY2027, management guided sales to $31.2–$31.8 billion (up ~1% at the midpoint, with Q1 down before a return to growth in H2), adjusted EBITDA of $730–$780 million (high single-digit growth, $25 million above the Investor Day target), and adjusted EPS of $3.00–$3.50 (~23% growth at the midpoint). The quarter reflected continued underlying sales growth in line with the $90 billion target market, offset by ~500 bps of optimization headwinds and ~150 bps from cycling short-term project work.

ServiceTitan reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue of $292.8 million, up 21% year-over-year, with platform revenue of $284.5 million (+22%), non-GAAP operating income of $44.4 million (15.2% margin, up 310 bps), and record free cash flow of $50.5 million (+47%). GTV grew 17% to $26.8 billion, about 200 bps below recent quarters due to lower existing-customer job growth, particularly in HVAC. Guidance for Q3 is $285-$287 million revenue and $29-$30 million operating income, with FY2027 revenue of $1.139-$1.144 billion and operating income of $152-$154 million, reflecting roughly $4-$5 million of near-term revenue headwinds from the Max mix shift and a more moderate GTV forecast. Management also narrowed its trade-expansion focus to existing trades and reported the CRO transition from Ross Biestman to Rikus Pretorius.

BrasilAgro reported FY2026 net revenue of BRL 926 million with adjusted EBITDA of BRL 100 million and a net loss of BRL 90 million, compared to a BRL 138 million loss in the prior year. Results were hurt by sugarcane fire/frost impacts and cotton quality issues, while soy and corn delivered volume and margin gains. Management did not provide explicit numeric guidance for FY2027 but pointed to backlog/pricing improvements (soy already locked above $12 versus $11) and expected farmland sales to recover recurring operational results. The company proposed BRL 30 million in dividends while prioritizing debt reduction given a high cost of capital (~14%).

NX reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $501.8 million, up 1.3% YoY, with volumes flat, pricing up ~3%, and a ~2% drag from IEEPA tariff reimbursements. Adjusted EPS rose to $0.79 from $0.69 and adjusted EBITDA edged up to $72.7 million from $70.3 million, though Extruded and Custom segment adjusted EBITDA both declined on inflationary pressure. Management guided Q4 revenue growth of 2%-3% and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 50-75 bps, while flagging mixed housing data: single-family completions down ~13% YoY but permits up 3% and authorized-not-started homes up ~10%.

Polestar reported Q2 2026 revenue of $727 million, down 8% year-on-year, with retail sales of roughly 17,300 cars down 4%, and a net loss of $459 million. Full-year volume guidance was cut to low to mid single-digit growth, and the company accepted the U.S. Department of Commerce decision barring model year 2027 sales in the U.S., triggering about $130 million in material adjustments tied to U.S. restructuring. Gross margin was negative 13% (adjusted negative 13%) versus negative 97% a year earlier, which was distorted by a $724 million impairment; operating and net losses narrowed largely because no such impairment recurred. Cash fell to $888 million from $1.159 billion at year-end 2025, with H1 operating cash outflow of $850 million.

Concrete Pumping Holdings reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $116.8 million, up 13% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA also up 13% to $30.4 million (26% margin) and net income of $4.5 million, or $0.09 per diluted share versus $0.07 a year ago. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $425-$435 million from $410-$425 million, adjusted EBITDA to $103-$108 million from $98-$105 million, and free cash flow to approximately $50 million from at least $45 million. The company also initiated a regular quarterly dividend of $0.13 per share (~5.6% annualized yield) and reduced net leverage to 3.6x from 3.8x. Positives were broad-based U.S. growth led by data centers and infrastructure plus 14% Eco-Pan growth; offsets included flat-to-down gross margin (38.7% vs. 39.0%), soft U.K. underlying demand, and continued weakness in residential and light commercial construction.

Q2 FY2027 revenue was $216.4 million, up 10% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance, with non-GAAP operating margin of 10% (up ~300 bps YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.10. NRR improved to 97% overall and 98% in both core ($5,000+) and $100,000+ cohorts, and AI Studio/AI Teammates drove ~25% of net new ARR. Q3 guidance of $217-219 million (8-9% growth) and full-year revenue of $858.5-863.5 million (9% growth) were framed against a rising PLG headwind (~100 bps in Q3, ~150 bps in Q4), a $1.2 million AWM revenue-timing impact, and ~150 bps of gross margin pressure as AI products are seeded into tiers. Full-year AI net-new-ARR target was raised to ~20% from ~15%, while FY2027 contribution from Client Management, Service Management and Command is assumed minimal.

Q2 net sales rose 10% to $1.611 billion with comps up 9%, adjusted operating income up 125% to $124 million and adjusted EPS nearly tripling to $0.95, both above the high end of guidance; adjusted gross margin expanded 320 bps to 38.8% on higher regular-price mix and lower promotions. Management raised full-year fiscal 2026 net sales guidance to $7.10-7.18 billion (8-10% growth vs prior 7-9%) and adjusted EPS to $4.45-4.70 from $4.35-4.60, while lifting adjusted operating income by $10 million at both ends. The raise was partly offset by plans to reinvest outperformance into marketing and by moderating back-half margin expansion, as Q4 promotions are planned flat to slightly down versus roughly 100 bps quarterly favorability in Q1-Q3.

PVH reported Q2 revenue down 3% in both reported and constant currency, at the high end of guidance and in line with all three regions, with operating margin of 11.1% and EPS of $3.70 ahead of plan; however, the quarter included approximately 510 basis points of operating margin benefit and about $1.80 of EPS from $107 million in tariff refunds, and excluding those refunds operating margin was 6% with EBIT of $126 million versus $178 million last year. Gross margin of 63% rose 530 basis points but was up only about 20 basis points excluding tariff refunds, and inventories fell 3%. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed at roughly flat reported revenue, ~8.8% operating margin, and $11.80-$12.10 EPS, with Q3 revenue guided down low single digits and Q3 operating margin of ~7.5%; EMEA remains pressured with the spring 2027 wholesale order book down mid-single digits, while Americas and APAC are expected to grow for the full year.

Planet reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $116M, up roughly 58% YoY, with non-GAAP gross margin of 59% and adjusted EBITDA of $13.9M, both above expectations; the beat was driven largely by point-in-time revenue from the Swedish Armed Forces satellite handover, which shifted revenue from Q3 into Q2. Full-year revenue guidance was raised at the low end to $430-441M (40-43% growth), gross margin guidance was lifted to 55-57%, and adjusted EBITDA guidance was also increased at the low end to $3-10M. Defense and intelligence grew over 90% YoY, commercial over 15%, and civil government over 5%, with EMEA revenue up over 130%. Q3 revenue guidance of $101-105M implies a sequential decline due to the timing of satellite services revenue, which management attributed to point-in-time recognition variability.

UiPath reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $410 million, up 13% YoY (16% normalized for an $8 million FX headwind), with ARR of $1.938 billion up 12% and net new ARR of $37 million versus $31 million in the prior quarter. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded over 400 bps YoY to 22%, delivering a fourth consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability, alongside a 97% gross retention rate and a net retention rate of 109%. Management guided Q3 revenue to $440-445 million and full-year FY2027 revenue to $1.789-1.794 billion, ARR to $2.065-2.070 billion, and non-GAAP operating income of approximately $445 million, maintaining its prudent guidance philosophy amid currency headwinds and a variable macro environment.

Oxford Industries reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $394M versus $403M a year ago, near the high end of the $380-400M guidance range, with adjusted EPS of $1.34 and adjusted gross margin expanding 140 bps to 63.1%; adjusted EBITDA was $45M (11.4% margin) versus $43M (10.7%). The company narrowed full-year sales guidance to $1.43-1.47B (down 3% to flat) from a prior slightly negative to slightly positive comp view, and cut adjusted EPS guidance to $1.60-2.00 from prior expectations, versus $2.11 last year, citing continued Lilly Pulitzer weakness and softer discretionary demand. Q3 is guided to a loss of $1.40-1.20 per share on $280-300M in sales, reflecting a mid- to low-single-digit negative comp, with gross margin expected to expand ~100 bps. Lilly Pulitzer's assortment challenges are now expected to persist through FY2026, with a substantial reset targeted for spring 2027.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $13.9 million, up 38.8% from $10 million in Q1, with gross margin expanding to 79.5% from 67.7%. Operating income turned positive at $1 million versus a $3.2 million loss in Q1, net income from continuing operations was $1.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.9 million from -$3.2 million. The $10.1 million digital assets platform plus A-MM revenue was slightly above the prior $9-$10 million outlook, but the company withdrew its previously issued financial guidance due to the strategic transition toward an agentic AI company, and will not provide updated guidance until it has more operating history. Management also said it is reviewing the structure and ownership of parts of its legacy financial services business, with nothing to announce.

Hello Group reported Q2 2026 total revenue of RMB 2.49 billion, down 5% year-over-year but up 4% sequentially, with domestic revenue down 17% YoY to RMB 1.81 billion and overseas revenue up 52% YoY to RMB 673 million (27% of total). Non-GAAP net income was RMB 273.9 million versus a RMB 96 million loss a year ago, while non-GAAP operating margin fell to 11.1% from 17.1%. Management guided Q3 revenue to RMB 2.4-2.5 billion (down 5.7% to 9.4% YoY, with domestic down high-teens and overseas up high-30s), revised its full-year group revenue decline to mid-single digits from a couple percent, and said the original RMB 3 billion 2026 overseas revenue target looks a stretch, likely RMB 100-200 million lower. The main negative change was a wider domestic revenue decline than previously expected due to weaker spending among top-tier live-streaming users.

Polestar Q2 2026 retail sales fell 4% YoY to ~17,300 cars and revenue dropped 8% YoY to $727 million, with adjusted gross margin deteriorating to negative 13% from negative 6% and adjusted EBITDA loss widening to $286 million from $206 million. On a reported basis the net loss of $459 million improved 55% YoY and operating loss fell 43% in H1, but largely because the prior period included $724 million of impairment charges. Management cut its full-year volume outlook to low to mid single-digit growth, absorbing a roughly $130 million hit from the U.S. BIS decision (which will halt sales of model-year 2027 vehicles in the U.S.) and continued pricing pressure, while pointing to Polestar 4 SUV and Polestar 5 launches as H2 drivers.

Fiscal Q2 FY2027 revenue was $108.1 million, slightly above the $105-111 million guidance midpoint and up 7.7% sequentially and 13.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 59.3% below the 59%-60.5% guidance midpoint and non-GAAP EPS of $0.18. Q3 guidance is $115-124 million (midpoint $119.5 million, roughly 10.5% sequential growth), with non-GAAP gross margin of 59%-60% and OpEx of $56.5-59.5 million. The company raised its five-year SAM to $22.9 billion by FY2032 (about 20% CAGR) and announced Capgemini and Macnica indirect-channel partnerships plus a new X7 AI accelerator sampling now, while flagging industry-wide memory cost inflation and supply scarcity as an uncertainty mainly for Q4. Automotive set a revenue record and the board authorized a new $50 million repurchase program.

Ciena reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.67 billion, up 37% year-on-year, at the top end of guidance. Adjusted gross margin reached 46.4% (up 450 basis points year-on-year, with a 70-basis-point tariff-refund benefit), adjusted operating margin hit a record 22.5% (250 basis points above the guide and more than double the year-ago level), and adjusted EPS was a record $2.11, up 215% year-on-year. The company raised its full-year revenue midpoint to $6.42 billion (up $120 million from last quarter) and issued preliminary FY2027 guidance for at least 30% revenue growth ($8.3-$8.4 billion), gross margin of at least 45%-46%, and adjusted operating margin of 25%-27%. Backlog rose $800 million to $8.5 billion, with management projecting over $10 billion by fiscal year-end and visibility extending into 2028.

Methode reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $265.4 million, up 10.4% year-over-year, driven by 27% industrial growth to $156.8 million on data center power distribution and off-road lighting, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $13.7 million from $15.7 million and the adjusted net loss was $0.22 per diluted share, matching the prior-year loss. The quarter included $6.7 million of one-time headwinds ($3.8 million portfolio refinements, $2.3 million premium freight), while underlying volume/mix/operational execution contributed a positive $4.7 million; SG&A rose to $45.9 million from $36.6 million on talent and professional fees. Automotive sales slipped 0.4% to $105.7 million and interface sales fell 73% to $2.9 million after the dataMate divestiture and an appliance program roll-off. Management reaffirmed fiscal 2027 guidance of $1.025-$1.075 billion net sales and $72-$82 million adjusted EBITDA (roughly 7%-7.6% margin) with free cash flow comparable to fiscal 2026, and booked $75 million of peak annual awards (~$400 million lifetime), mostly hybrid automotive programs launching late next fiscal year.

Duluth Trading reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $121.4 million, down 7.8% year-over-year, with reported and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.50 including $16.3 million in tariff refunds that contributed $0.44 per share. Excluding tariff refunds, underlying gross margin expanded 490 basis points to 59.6%, adjusted EBITDA was $10.7 million (8.8% of sales), and free cash flow improved $41 million to $13 million, with inventory down 15.5% and clearance inventory down 43.1%. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $38-$42 million from $28-$32 million, but that increase is driven by the $16.3 million tariff refund; net sales guidance was reaffirmed at $540-$560 million, with Q3 expected to soften as the company laps prior-year clearance events and Q4 improving sequentially. The top-line decline reflects the intentional promotional reset and SKU rationalization, with women's product sales down 15% and AKHG down 26%.

Docusign reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $876M (up 9% YoY, with a 1.3pp FX tailwind) and non-GAAP operating income of $277M (32% margin, up 180bps YoY, beating the guidance midpoint by 160bps). Non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 26% YoY to $1.16, free cash flow was $296M (34% margin, up over 35% YoY), and the company repurchased $307M of stock. Full-year revenue guidance of $3.499–$3.507B incorporates the Q2 beat plus second-half outperformance, partially offset by a $4M FX headwind, while full-year ARR growth guidance was raised to 8.5–9.0% (from 8.0% prior) and IAM is now expected to represent 18–19% of exiting Q4 ARR versus 15.1% in Q2. Reported non-GAAP gross margin was 81.7%, down slightly YoY due to cloud migration, and IAM ARR grew sequentially from 12.6% to 15.1% of total ARR.

BRP reported Q2 FY2027 revenues of CAD 2.2 billion, up 18% year over year, with normalized EBITDA of CAD 139 million and a normalized loss per share of CAD 0.18, results that came in ahead of expectations despite an incremental net tariff headwind of about CAD 145 million. Gross margin fell to 11.7%, reflecting roughly 740 basis points of tariff impact and a 330 basis point one-time supplier restructuring charge, though excluding these items gross margin would have expanded about 140 basis points. Management raised full-year normalized EPS guidance by CAD 1 to CAD 4.00-CAD 4.50, with revenue of CAD 9.225-CAD 9.475 billion and normalized EBITDA of CAD 1.025-CAD 1.075 billion, citing ORV momentum and lower net tariff exposure of CAD 200 million for the year versus prior assumptions. The quarter also included the announcement of CFO Sébastien Martel's retirement and the appointment of Minh Thanh Tran as incoming CFO, plus a decision to cut personal watercraft shipments for the balance of the year due to softer industry demand.

Q2 FY2027 revenue fell 3% to $530 million with overall comps down 1%, driven by store closures, the license exit ahead of the Wrangler launch, and a 9% schuh comp decline from reduced promotions. Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 bps to 47.2% and adjusted operating loss improved $6 million to a loss of $8 million, with adjusted diluted loss per share of $0.83 versus $1.14 last year. Management raised the full-year EPS outlook to the high end of its $2.00-$2.40 range from the middle, but cut the full-year comp assumption to flat from up 1%-2% and now guides total sales down about 2%, citing more promotional U.K. market conditions, marketing investment, and $14 million of licensed-exit sales pressure in Q3. Q3 operating income is expected moderately below last year, with earnings growth resuming in Q4.

Samsara reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $508 million, up 30% year-over-year, with ending ARR of $2.1 billion (also +30% YoY) and net new ARR of $134 million, up 28% YoY in constant currency. GAAP EPS turned positive at $0.03 (fourth consecutive GAAP profitable quarter) and non-GAAP operating margin reached 21%, up 6 percentage points YoY. The company guided Q3 revenue to $514-516 million (24% YoY growth) and FY2027 revenue to $2.043-2.047 billion (26% YoY growth), while noting FCF margin will be ~100bps lower than FY2026 due to inventory pre-buys and supply chain costs. Large customer metrics accelerated: $100k+ ARR customers grew 38% YoY (fourth straight quarter of sequential acceleration) and $1M+ ARR customers grew over 50% YoY.

Lands' End reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $302 million, up 3% year-over-year, with a 9% increase in U.S. e-commerce (helped by a Q1 order backlog catch-up, though the U.S. business is flattish year-to-date), a 4% rise in Outfitters, and approximately flat Europe. Gross margin expanded about 320 basis points to 52%, driven by an IEEPA tariff refund, while adjusted net income was $2.7 million ($0.09 per share) and adjusted EBITDA fell $4 million to $11 million, reflecting the new WHP JV royalty structure and warehouse management system challenges in value-added services. Third quarter guidance calls for revenue of $300-$330 million and EPS of $0.07-$0.20; full-year fiscal 2026 guidance is $1.3-$1.35 billion in revenue and $0.44-$0.72 in EPS, incorporating current tariffs. The quarter marked the first earnings call under new CEO Charlie Cole, with a $100 million buyback authorization (about $11 million repurchased, $89 million remaining) and a 13% inventory increase described as normalized.
