Lululemon reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue down 4% (or 5% in constant currency) to $2.4 billion, with comparable sales down 10%; North America fell 8% and China mainland grew 4% (down 2% constant currency), both below expectations. Gross margin expanded 200 bps to 60.5% (benefiting from 560 bps of IEEPA tariff refunds), but operating margin fell to 18.8% from 20.7%, and GAAP EPS was $2.92 versus $3.10 (including an $0.86 tariff-refund benefit). Management lowered full-year guidance to revenue of $10.35-$10.5 billion (down 5-7%), operating margin down approximately 530 bps, and EPS of $9.48-$9.73 versus $13.26 in 2025, citing brand-sentiment issues, a slow start to Q3, inconsistent new-product response, and a leg-gings decline of roughly 20%. The company also cut net new store openings to about 35 from 40 and accelerated expense actions.

Toro reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 8.4% to $1.23 billion (6.2% organic) with adjusted EPS of $1.33, and both professional (+8.8%) and residential (+8.6%) segments grew over 8%. Adjusted operating margin was 13.9% (+30 bps), with residential margin up 400 bps to 5.9% while professional margin fell 40 bps to 20.9%. The company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.60-$4.65 from $4.50-$4.62 (midpoint up $0.07 to $4.63) and lifted net sales growth guidance to 6.3%-6.6% from 4.0%-6.5%. Free cash flow was $425 million at 128% conversion, with $358 million of share repurchases; an unfavorable tax rate (22.4%) and a $43 million non-cash impairment partially offset the quarter.

Mama's Creations reported Q2 FY2027 revenue up 55% to $54.6 million and adjusted EBITDA up 68.9% to $5.5 million (10.1% margin), with net income more than doubling to $2.6 million or $0.06 per diluted share. Gross margin of 24.0% improved sequentially from 23.6% but declined from 24.9% a year ago, while operating expenses fell 160 basis points to 18.5% of revenue. Management cited new Kroger distribution (Louisville division, 100+ stores, four items starting next month) and a larger Costco MVM across all eight regions as forward drivers, and reaffirmed a mid-to-high 20% gross margin target. The company ended the quarter with $138.6 million in cash and $4.8 million of total debt; explicit EPS guidance was not provided.

Wiley reported Q1 FY2027 revenue with research up 4% to $293M (Research Publishing +12%, including $13M from Emerald) but learning down 20% to $93M. Adjusted EPS fell 10% and GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.23 versus $0.22 prior year, largely due to restructuring and acquisition costs. The year-over-year decline was driven by a known $29M prior-year AI licensing comparison, though AI revenue of $14M was realized and the company reaffirmed full-year guidance of low-to-mid single-digit organic growth and adjusted EPS of $4.60-$5.05. Management highlighted strong publishing KPIs, margin expansion in research, and early momentum in new partnerships, while acknowledging continued softness in learning.

Smith & Wesson reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $112.6 million, up 32.3% YoY, with gross margin of 28.7% (up 2.8 points, 260 bps from $2.9 million of tariff refunds) and EPS of $0.06 versus a $0.08 loss last year; adjusted EBITDAS grew 86%. Q1 shipments grew roughly 20% against 7.7% adjusted NICS growth, with channel inventories flat and long-gun inventories down 5,000 units, indicating share gains. Management guided Q2 sales to roughly 10% above last year and Q2 gross margin 200-300 bps higher YoY, but left the full-year revenue growth outlook unchanged at 5%-7%, implying a back-half deceleration versus the 32% Q1 growth. Capital spending is expected at $45-$50 million for the year, and the board declared a $0.13 quarterly dividend.

American Outdoor Brands reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $37.3 million, up 25.4% YoY (about 4% excluding last year's $6 million order pull-forward), with gross margin of 53% up 630 bps and non-GAAP EPS of $0.03 versus a $0.26 loss a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $4.3 million from a loss, and the company ended with $33.3 million cash and no debt. Management maintained FY2027 net sales guidance of $200-$210 million but raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $14.5-$17.5 million from roughly $13-$16 million, citing strong new-product mix (36% of Q1 sales) and e-com channel strength; Q2 net sales are guided to rise about 3%. New products contributed 36% of net sales versus a historical 20-25%, though tariffs are expected to pressure gross margin beginning in Q3.

Zscaler reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $898M, up 25% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with total ARR of $3.8B also up 25% and a record non-GAAP operating margin of 24.3% (up 220 bps YoY). Net new ARR was $246M (up 24%), or $232M (up 17%) excluding Red Canary, which marked a sequential acceleration from 7% in FY2025 and 10% in the first half of FY2026. FY2027 guidance calls for revenue of $3.908B-$3.938B (16.6%-17.5% growth), ARR of $4.396B-$4.426B (~16.6%-17.4%), an operating margin of ~23.7%, EPS of $4.86-$4.90, and a free cash flow margin of 23%-23.5%; the ARR growth guide implies a step-down from Q4's 25% pace, reflecting the sales leadership transition and timing of the new Agentic SecOps launch. Management also announced a restructuring affecting ~3% of employees with $30M-$33M in charges, and expects elevated CapEx in FY2027 on higher memory and component pricing.

Matrix Service reported fiscal Q4 2026 revenue of $244.5 million, up 13% from $216.4 million, with GAAP EPS of $0.04 versus a $0.40 loss and adjusted EPS of $0.16 versus a $0.28 loss; gross margin expanded to 8.0% from 3.8% and SG&A fell to $16.9 million from $17.6 million. However, the company swung to a $0.9 million operating loss including $3.4 million of restructuring costs, and Q4 bookings of $169 million produced a 0.7 book-to-bill, leaving backlog at $953 million after prior declines. Management provided no guidance, citing the CFO transition, though it said backlog is supportive of strong fiscal 2027 revenue with 70-80% expected to be worked off during the year and margins trending toward double digits. The quarter reflects a return to profitability under the Win, Execute, Deliver strategy but mixed award activity, and the absence of formal guidance adds uncertainty.

Guidewire reported Q4 FY2026 ARR of $1.242B, up 19% YoY on constant currency and above the high end of guidance, with fully ramped ARR up 22%, subscription and support revenue up 33% to $971M for the year, and total FY2026 revenue of $1.475B, up 23%. FY2026 operating income of $340M rose 63% YoY and beat the outlook, with subscription and support gross margin of 74.5%, up four points. FY2027 guidance calls for ARR of $1.45-1.46B (18% constant-currency growth at the midpoint), total revenue of $1.707-1.727B, and subscription and support gross margin of 75-76%; the ARR guide assumes attrition normalizes from record lows versus FY2026.

eGain reported Q4 FY2026 total revenue of $22.2 million, exceeding guidance and Street consensus but down from $23.2 million a year ago, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.08 also above guidance and consensus and adjusted EBITDA of $2.2 million. Full-year revenue rose 3% to $91.1 million with AI customer revenue up 20%, record operating cash flow of $21.2 million, and $11.5 million of buybacks, while GAAP net income of $8.9 million fell sharply from the prior year's $32.3 million that included a $29 million tax benefit. FY2027 guidance called for total revenue of $84.5-$86 million, implying a decline, as an expected 40% drop in legacy customer revenue more than offsets roughly 20% AI customer ARR growth and 8-10% AI customer revenue growth. Net dollar-based retention fell to 93% for all customers from 105%, total SaaS ARR declined 1% year-over-year, and RPO was down 5% to $87 million.

Campbell's Q4 FY2026 discussion centered on weak guidance: organic net sales guided down ~3% and adjusted EPS of $1.65-$1.80, with Q1 gross margin down significantly and EPS declining sharply before turning positive only by Q4. Management disclosed a $500M cost-savings program (FY2027-FY2030), a ~4-5% price increase on ~60% of the portfolio starting Q2, and a dividend reduction described as 'necessary.' Snacks is the key drag, with Q1 snacks sales guided down high single digits and consumption recovery not expected to reach positive.

Brady closed FY2026 with record Q4 revenue and adjusted EPS, with organic sales up 8.4%, acquisitions adding 1.1%, and FX adding 0.5% for 10% total growth; adjusted diluted EPS rose 17.5% to $1.48 versus $1.26, and GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.96 from $1.04. Gross margin improved to 52.9% from 50.4% (aided by a ~$4 million tariff refund), and operating cash flow rose 35.8% to $79.2 million; the company also announced its 41st consecutive dividend increase. For FY2027, management guided to $6.25–$6.75 adjusted diluted EPS, including ~$0.80 of IPS accretion, with IDS organic growth of ~5% and IPS revenue of ~$1.15 billion. This is the first quarter reflecting the renamed segments (IDS and IPS) following the Honeywell PSS acquisition close, with IPS expected to be immediately accretive.

VersaBank reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of CAD 38.8 million (up 23% year-over-year, 1% sequentially), net income of CAD 10.1 million (up 53% YoY), and adjusted net income of CAD 12.3 million or CAD 0.38 per share (up 27% YoY). U.S. banking revenue grew 199% YoY and 18% sequentially to CAD 9.3 million with net income up 803% YoY to CAD 3.9 million. NIM compressed to 2.44% on credit assets (down 11 bps YoY, 27 bps sequentially), with management guiding NIM back to ~2.30% next quarter and reiterating a U.S. SRP target of $3 billion in fiscal 2027. Total assets surpassed CAD 7 billion post-quarter, and the company expects core non-interest expenses to remain flat in fiscal 2027 despite significant asset growth.

Torrid reported Q2 net sales of $231.7 million, down from $262.8 million a year ago, with comparable sales down 6.3%; adjusted EBITDA was $23.3 million, but only $12.1 million (5.2% margin) excluding an $11.1 million IEEPA tariff refund, within guidance. Gross margin was 38.7% versus 35.6% a year ago, but 33.9% excluding the tariff refund, down 170 basis points on targeted promotions. GAAP net income was $5.2 million, or $0.05 per share, versus $1.6 million or $0.02 last year, and SG&A declined $8.6 million to $61.9 million on store-optimization savings. Full-year net sales guidance was maintained at $940-$960 million, while adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $76-$86 million solely to reflect the tariff refund; excluding it, the $65-$75 million outlook is unchanged, and management expects a return to positive comparable sales in the second half.

Gold.com reported fiscal Q4 2026 revenue up 99% to $5.0 billion (about $0.9 billion from forward sales) and gross profit up 35% to $110.3 million, or 2.2% of revenue versus 3.25% a year ago, while net income was $12.2 million and diluted EPS was $0.41, flat versus the prior year. Full-year revenue rose 132% to $25.5 billion, gross profit rose 115% to $453.1 million, and net income was $82.3 million or $3.02 per diluted share; Q4 EBITDA fell 3% to $28.2 million even as adjusted net income rose 29% to $24.7 million. Management disclosed a mid-March to early-April demand slowdown that continued through Q4 and into the first two months of fiscal 2027, noted higher rates pressuring metal prices and silver premiums narrowing, and said new DTC customers fell 38% year over year to 67,900. No explicit fiscal 2027 revenue or EPS guidance was provided; management announced a $1.00 special dividend alongside the regular $0.20 dividend and left M&A and buybacks open-ended.

Brown-Forman reported Q1 FY2027 organic net sales declined about 1%, following roughly 9% growth in the trailing Q4, with gross margin up 40 bps to 60.2%, reported operating income down 3% but organic operating income up 4%, and EPS up 6% to $0.38. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance of approximately flat organic net sales and a 3%-5% organic operating income decline, but said confidence has increased that results will trend toward the more favorable end of the operating income range. Growth from New Mix, the broader RTD portfolio, and Jack Daniel's Tennessee Blackberry was offset by a more than 60% decline in used barrel sales, a low-teens decline in the full-strength tequila portfolio, and an 8% organic net sales decline in developed international markets, with U.S. shipments trailing depletions by about 4 points. Because it is early in a rocky year, management gave no quantitative raise despite the improved operating income confidence.

Daktronics reported Q1 FY2027 net sales up 7.1% and EPS of $0.40, up 21.2% and the highest quarterly EPS in three years, despite the quarter having one fewer week than the prior-year period. Gross margin rose 80 bps to 30.5% and operating income grew 7.2% to $24.9 million, aided by about $3 million in tariff refunds largely offset by rising raw material costs. Order bookings were down year over year and backlog fell to $311 million from $356 million, which management attributed to order timing and said sizable projects would book in Q2. FY2028 targets (7%-10% revenue CAGR, 10%-12% operating margin, 17%-20% ROIC) were reaffirmed, and the company disclosed NBA and SEC information requests.

C3.ai reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $52.4 million, with subscription revenue of $49.2 million (94% of total), non-GAAP gross margin improving sequentially to 50% from 37%, non-GAAP operating loss of $36.2 million ($8.3 million better than the midpoint of guidance), and positive free cash flow of $2.1 million versus negative $34.3 million a year ago. Bookings grew 73% with federal bookings up 138%, and restructuring delivered roughly $135 million in annualized cost savings including a ~40% headcount reduction. Guidance was set at $51-55 million revenue and a $34.5-42.5 million non-GAAP operating loss for Q2, and $210-240 million revenue with a $123-155 million non-GAAP operating loss for FY2027; gross margin is expected to moderate to the mid-40s next quarter on forward-deployed engineering investment. Revenue was above guidance but the forward outlook was not raised and the CEO emphasized consistent quarter-over-quarter growth over hitting the high end of the range.

Broadcom reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $29.6B, up 86% YoY, with AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7B up 221% YoY and 54% sequentially; non-GAAP EPS was $3.32, up 96% YoY, and operating margin hit a record 67.9%, though gross margin fell 210 bps sequentially to 75% on AI mix. Q4 guidance calls for $34.8B revenue (+93% YoY) and AI revenue of $21.7B (+236% YoY), and management introduced multiyear AI revenue targets of ~$115B in FY2027 and ~$230B in FY2028, citing secured supply. Fiscal 2026 AI revenue guidance was lifted to $58B from a prior $56B, the key change versus the prior period, alongside an agreement with Google to supply tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually. Non-AI semiconductor revenue was $4.2B, up 5% YoY, and infrastructure software was $8.8B, up 29% YoY, with Q4 software guided to ~$8.7B.

HPE reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $12.2B, up 34% YoY, exceeding the high end of guidance, with record non-GAAP gross margin of 40%, record operating profit of $2B, 16.2% operating margin (up 290 bps sequentially), and record non-GAAP EPS of $1.11, the first time above $1. Free cash flow was a Q3 record $958M, and management raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $3.75-$3.85 and the FCF target to at least $3.75B. The company also raised its FY2027 framework to revenue growth of 13%-17% and EPS of $4.40-$4.60, supported by record backlog, orders up 42% normalized, and strong AI and networking demand, though supply constraints persist and gross margin is expected to moderate toward historical levels.

Total Q3 FY2026 revenue was $33 million, down 29% from $46.7 million a year ago, with a gross loss of $24.5 million versus a $5.1 million gross loss prior year, driven by $17 million of Fit Energy Phase Zero charges ($4 million inventory write-down plus $13 million firm purchase commitment losses). Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $45.3 million, or $0.64 per share, versus $92.5 million, or $3.78 per share, and adjusted EBITDA was -$36.7 million versus -$16.4 million. Committed backlog was $1.3 billion, up 4.1% year-over-year, with a new $2.4 billion awarded capacity backlog category (Fit Energy phases 1-3, 350 MW) for total $3.6 billion, and a 75 MW capacity reservation with a colocation data center operator was closed after quarter end. Management set a new target of positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 FY2027, dependent on converting awarded capacity to committed contracts, reaching 100 MW annualized production by October 2026, and cost reductions; no revenue or EPS guidance was given.

Argan reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $384 million, up 62% YoY, with record net income of $53.3 million ($3.76 per diluted share) and record adjusted EBITDA of $70 million (18.2% margin). Gross margin was 19.3% versus 18.6% a year ago but down from 21.0% in Q1 and 25% in Q4 FY2026, reflecting earlier-stage power project revenues; power gross margin was 22.4% and industrial 7.3% on cost overruns. Consolidated backlog fell to $2.5 billion from $2.9 billion at the start of fiscal year, though management cited a strong pipeline and expects to add a handful of new projects over the next 7-15 months, with full-year FY2027 revenue significantly above FY2026. The quarter included the ValCor Communications acquisition, a quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share, and approximately $1 billion in cash and investments with no debt.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $63.5 million, up 6.9% year over year and in line with guidance, with gross margin of 37.4%, up 120 basis points from 36.2% a year earlier despite higher memory costs. Adjusted operating loss widened to $11.1 million from $4.9 million a year ago, driven by an $8.4 million OpEx increase (including $2.9 million of product-launch marketing) and FX headwinds. Q3 revenue guidance of $68-73 million implies a 4-10% year-over-year decline against a $75.8 million prior-year base, attributed to supply constraints on Helio Strap/Balance 3/Bip, launch timing, and macro softness, though the company expects to return to growth in Q4. Management also announced Bip family price increases starting January 2027 to offset entry-level cost pressure.

Total net revenues rose 5.1% YoY to RMB 1.14 billion, driven by a 40.4% increase in skincare (now 71.5% of revenue) but offset by a 35.8% decline in color cosmetics. Gross margin fell to 73.9% from 78.3% on higher color-cosmetics inventory provisions, watching and marketing rose to 70.7% of revenue from 66.5%, and the company swung to a net loss of RMB 90.8 million from a RMB 19.5 million loss, with non-GAAP net loss of RMB 99.4 million versus prior-year non-GAAP income of RMB 11.5 million. Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of RMB 898.6-998.4 million, a 0-10% YoY decline, following the more moderate-than-expected Q2 growth.

NTAP reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $2.03B, up 30% YoY (26% ex-extra week) and 4% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.58, up 66% YoY, exceeding the high end of guidance on every metric. Gross margin was 70.6%, down 50 bps YoY on product mix but above guidance, and operating margin reached 31.9%, up 6.1 points YoY. The company raised FY27 revenue guidance to $7.975B-$8.225B (17% YoY growth at $8.1B midpoint, an increase of $650M vs prior guidance) and raised EPS guidance to $9.73-$10.03 (22% YoY growth at $9.88 midpoint). Management cited broad-based momentum in public cloud (+28% YoY), all-flash arrays (+47% YoY), and AI-related deals (approximately 350 deals), while acknowledging some accelerated purchases and improved pricing that are not expected to repeat at the same level.

Netskope reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $220.5 million, up 29% year-over-year and ahead of guidance, with ARR of $899 million (up 27%), net new ARR of $54 million (up 9%), and NRR rising to 114%. Gross margin was 77% (up ~2 points), operating margin improved 11 points year-over-year to -9% versus guidance, and EPS loss of $0.03 beat. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $888-892 million (~26% growth), with the raise slightly exceeding the Q2 beat, though Q3 revenue growth is guided to decelerate to ~24%. The company also announced a ~5% workforce reduction and is transitioning customers to annual billings.

Sprinklr reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue of $213.7 million, up 1% year-over-year, with subscription revenue up 3% to $194.8 million and non-GAAP operating income of $31.3 million (15% margin, $0.11 EPS). Professional services revenue of $18.9 million came in below expectations on managed services softness and partner cost overruns, driving services gross margin to -22% and total non-GAAP gross margin to 66%. For FY2027, the company raised its subscription revenue guide to $782.5-$784.5 million (4% growth) while keeping total revenue at $866.5-$868.5 million (1% growth) and non-GAAP operating income at $139-$141 million; Q3 total revenue is guided to $215-$216 million, slightly down year-over-year on a 34% decline in professional services. Total RPO was $1.03 billion, up 11% year-over-year, and the $125 million accelerated share repurchase was completed with $75 million remaining under the authorization.

G-III reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $555 million, down 10% YoY and slightly below plan, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.26 ahead of the $0.15-$0.25 guidance range; gross margin expanded 440 bps to 45.2% on price actions and a mix shift to owned brands. Full-year net sales guidance was reiterated at approximately $2.71 billion, while non-GAAP EPS guidance was raised to $2.20-$2.30 from a prior range, as Q3 revenue is guided to about $870 million versus $989 million last year due to the largest PVH license exit. The company closed the Marc Jacobs acquisition and owns 100% of the operating company plus a 50% stake in the IP joint venture with WHP; it guides to ~$360 million in Marc Jacobs sales this year and expects the deal to be dilutive for the first 12 months before turning accretive. Balance sheet is strong with $529 million in cash, aided by $134 million in tariff refunds, and inventories down 13% YoY.

Ollie's reported Q2 FY2026 net sales up 9.1% to $741 million on 15 new stores, but comparable store sales fell 1.8% against a challenging multiyear stack due to weather, promotional pressure, and a cautious consumer. Gross margin rose 360 bps to 43.5%, though the entire increase—and more—came from 380 bps of IEEPA tariff refunds; adjusted EPS jumped 43% to $1.42 and adjusted EBITDA rose 36% to $127 million. Management lowered full-year sales and comp guidance (comp now flat to +0.5% vs prior expectations) while raising the buyback authorization to $175 million and planning about $50 million in price investments for the year. The quarter's earnings strength was largely refund-driven, and the forward outlook is more measured than previously communicated.

Phreesia reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $129.5 million, up 10% year-over-year but down about 1% sequentially, with Adjusted EBITDA of $32.9 million (25% margin) and net income of $1.9 million, its fifth consecutive positive net income quarter. Average healthcare services clients rose to 4,744, up 36 sequentially and 277 year-over-year, while total revenue per AHSC of $27,289 rose 4% year-over-year but fell about 2% sequentially on payment processing seasonality. Management maintained its FY2027 revenue outlook of $510-$520 million and Adjusted EBITDA outlook of $125-$135 million, and continued to expect mid-single-digit AHSC growth and low-single-digit revenue per AHSC growth. The company reduced debt principal by over $23 million and generated $18.3 million in operating cash flow and $13.8 million in free cash flow, though commentary indicated some subscription revenue is being moderated to support downstream network and payments growth.

REX reported Q2 net sales of $168.5 million versus $158.6 million a year ago, with gross profit of $53.3 million versus $14.3 million, aided by $18.4 million in 45Z production tax credit income. Net income attributable to REX was $34.9 million or a record second-quarter $1.06 per diluted share, compared to $7.1 million or $0.22 per share. Management said it expects to remain profitable in Q3 and for results to be better than the prior-year period, while the One Earth ethanol expansion stays on track for completion by end-2026 and the carbon capture project received draft EPA Class VI well permits in August. Versus the prior period, margins expanded sharply on stronger crush margins and tax credits, though SG&A rose to $15.6 million from $6.2 million on higher incentive compensation and restricted stock awards.

Snowflake reported Q2 FY2027 product revenue of $1.49 billion, up 37% year-over-year — its third consecutive quarter of acceleration — and non-GAAP operating margin of 15%, expanding over 400 basis points year-over-year. Net revenue retention was 126%, RPO grew 30% to $9 billion, and the company added 692 net new customers (up 32% YoY). Management raised FY2027 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion (36% YoY growth, a 500+ bps increase), lifted non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 14.5% from 13.5%, and guided Q3 product revenue to $1.588–1.593 billion (37–38% YoY). Non-GAAP product gross margin guidance was lowered to 74% due to a higher mix of lower-margin AI workloads, and adjusted free cash flow margin guidance was reiterated at 23%.

ChargePoint reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $116 million, above its $100-$110 million guidance range, up 18% year-over-year and 14% sequentially, marking a fourth consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Non-GAAP gross margin was 38%, including ~$4 million of one-time tariff refunds; normalized gross margin was 35%, up 3 points sequentially and 2 points YoY. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5 million from $19 million in Q1 and $22 million a year ago, with cash of $96 million and essentially zero cash burn. Q3 guidance is $105-$115 million revenue (about 4% YoY growth at the midpoint), with gross margin expected to remain near normalized levels and OpEx below $50 million per quarter; management noted the Q2 revenue beat was partly driven by lumpy higher home sales not expected to repeat.

Tilly's reported Q2 FY2026 total net sales of $163.5 million, up 8.1%, with comparable net sales up 12.1% — a third consecutive quarter of double-digit comps. Gross margin expanded 300 basis points to 35.5%, net income was $8.4 million or $0.27 per diluted share versus $0.10 last year, and the company returned to trailing-four-quarter and year-to-date profitability for the first time since 2022. Management guided Q3 net sales to $150–$155 million (10–14% comps) and EPS of $0.07–$0.12 versus last year's $0.05 loss, while noting bonus accrual headwinds and that September comps decelerated about 8 points after back-to-school in three of the last four years.

rows.company_name: Petco Health and Wellness Co Inc
rows.key_quote: Petco reported Q2 net sales of $1.5 billion, up slightly year over year, with a 0.6% comp representing a second consecutive quarter of positive comps. Adjusted EBITDA was $122 million (8.2% of sales), including a $6.8 million net tariff refund; normalized Adjusted EBITDA of $115 million came in above the prior-year level and above the company's outlook. Gross margin expanded 37 basis points to 39.7% but was roughly flat excluding the tariff benefit, and full-year guidance was affirmed at flat to +1.5% net sales and $415-$430 million Adjusted EBITDA, with Q3 sales growth guided to 0.4%-1% and Q3 Adjusted EBITDA of $100-$103 million. The membership relaunch drove point redemptions that exceeded projections and reduced Q2 net sales by a mid-single-digit-million amount, which management said is now behind them.

Five Below reported Q2 FY2027 net sales up 23% to $1.3 billion, with comparable sales growth of 14% and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.68, more than double last year's $0.68. Adjusted operating margin expanded 360 basis points to 9.0%, and gross margin rose 220 basis points to 35.6%. Management raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to sales of $5.63-$5.71 billion (19% growth) and adjusted EPS of $10.07 (51% growth), up from prior outlook. A new $600 million share repurchase authorization was approved, and Q3 guidance was set at $1.21-$1.23 billion in sales with 8-10% comps and EPS of $1.07.

Sasol reported FY2026 adjusted EBITDA up 17% to ZAR 61 billion, with sales volumes up 4%, cash fixed costs flat, capex down 18% to ZAR 21 billion, and free cash flow of ZAR 11.9 billion (up 26% excluding the prior-year Transnet benefit). Net debt fell 11% to $3.3 billion, ahead of the below $3.7 billion target, and the Southern African oil breakeven improved to $49/bbl on a five-year-high Secunda production of 7.26 million tons. Guidance remains unchanged on the path to net debt below $3 billion sustainably between FY2027 and FY2028, though working capital came in above target at 18.3% and chemical markets remain below historical levels.

Cango reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of ~$50.8 million, with ~$47.4 million from Bitcoin mining (656 BTC mined), roughly 50% lower sequentially versus Q1's ~$100M+ due to a deliberate hash rate reduction. Net loss was ~$81.6 million, driven mainly by a $42.9 million mining machine impairment and an $8.5 million disposal loss. Cash mining cost fell to $73,313 per Bitcoin (down ~35% QoQ), with all-in cost of $98,405, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $10.7 million. Management gave no formal guidance but expects AI-related revenue (first customer contract signed post-June 30) to begin in Q3 and said mining hash rate should be roughly stable in Q3, aside from possible summer power curtailment.

NIO reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of RMB 32.1 billion, up 69.1% year-over-year and 25.9% quarter-over-quarter, with vehicle sales of RMB 29.1 billion (up 80.1% YoY) on 107,658 deliveries (+49.4% YoY). Vehicle margin was 18.5% versus 10.3% a year ago and 18.8% last quarter, and overall gross margin was 18.4% versus 10.0% last year and 19.0% last quarter. Adjusted net profit was RMB 26.1 million and cash rose to RMB 56.7 billion with positive operating and free cash flow. Q3 delivery guidance is 108,000-111,000 units and Q4 is targeted at over 40,000 units per month, while management expects Q3/Q4 vehicle margin to hold near Q2 levels despite RMB 2,000-3,000 per car of additional material cost pressure.

Rezolve Ai reported H1 FY2026 revenue of $130.8 million, up approximately 1,970% from $6.3 million in H1 2025, with a customer base expanding to over 1,640 from roughly 950 at year-end. Gross profit was $63.9 million (48.9% margin), while the reported operating loss widened to $128.1 million and adjusted EBITDA loss was $32.6 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of approximately $360 million—implying roughly $229 million in H2—and reiterated its target of at least $500 million in ARR exiting the year, citing seasonal H2 weighting, a larger customer base, and partner-led distribution. The company ended the period with $33.2 million in cash plus $67.4 million restricted cash, after raising approximately $250 million in gross equity capital during the half.

Sibanye reported record 1H revenue and EBITDA more than doubled, with South Africa PGM AISC margin of 44% on a 67% higher basket and SA gold adjusted EBITDA a record ZAR 9 billion, up 87% at a 39% margin. Group net operating cash was a record, debt was reduced, and a dividend was maintained at a 25-35% payout. U.S. PGM adjusted EBITDA fell 56% YoY to $66 million on the prior-year 45X credit, while recycling and Century zinc delivered strong cash conversion. The board approved Burnstone and Mt Lyell projects, but Stillwater union labor agreements remain unresolved and gold costs were guided to ZAR 1.75-1.84 million/kg for the second half.

Palo Alto Networks reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $3.41 billion, up 34%, and full-year revenue of $11.5 billion, up 24%. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.02, exceeding the high end of guidance by $0.04, and Q4 RPO reached $21.2 billion (up 34%) with NGS ARR at $9.1 billion (up 63%). The company exceeded guidance across all metrics and management said FY2027 guidance is set to exceed consensus, but gross margin declined 100 bps to 74.8% on SaaS mix and rising memory/storage costs.

GitLab reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $286.3 million, up 21% year-over-year and roughly five points ahead of guidance, with Non-GAAP operating income of $42.6 million (15% margin). Net ARR grew 42% year-over-year, the strongest gross bookings quarter in company history, and dollar-based net retention rose to 117%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.129-$1.133 billion (18%-19% growth) and Non-GAAP EPS to $0.85-$0.87, citing broad-based strength and public sector recovery. The quarter included the launch of the Flex consumption model, which is expected to introduce near-term revenue recognition timing noise but is not included in guidance.

Credo reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $479 million, up 10% sequentially and 115% year over year, above the high end of guidance, with non-GAAP gross margin of 68%, non-GAAP net income of $236.3 million (up 4% sequentially and more than doubling YoY), and a 48.2% non-GAAP operating margin. Q2 guidance is $525-535 million with gross margin of 67-69%, and full-year FY2027 revenue growth is reiterated at more than 85% with optical revenue exceeding $600 million. The key change versus prior periods is the emergence of optics as a second growth engine via DustPhotonics PIC revenue and ZeroFlap ramp, while cash fell $679 million on the DustPhotonics acquisition and Q1 operating cash flow declined $92 million sequentially to $90.2 million on working capital.

Medtronic reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $9.8 billion, up 13.7% organic, and adjusted EPS of $1.45, $0.06 above the midpoint of guidance and consensus. The quarter benefited from an extra watching week that added roughly $570 million, or 670 bps, to organic growth; excluding it, management called it the strongest quarterly performance in nearly eight years. Guidance was raised: FY2027 organic revenue growth to 7.25%-7.75% (up 50 bps) and EPS to $5.94-$6.00, with Q2 organic growth of ~6% and EPS of $1.32-$1.34. Adjusted gross margin was 65.2% (+10 bps) and adjusted operating margin 23.7% (+10 bps), with FY operating margin expansion guided to ~50 bps.

Q1 FY2027 revenue was $843 million, up 15.8% organic, with U.S. growth accelerating to 13.1% from 1.5% in Q4 and international up 16.9%; the extra week added about 4.6 points, leaving low-double-digit underlying growth versus 8.7% in Q4. Adjusted EBITDA was $83 million (9.9% margin), depressed about 230 bps by an $8 million pull-forward of Flex/Fit investment and a $12 million FX remeasurement charge; excluding these, margin was 12.2%, with adjusted gross margin at 55.9% and Simplera yields trending better than modeled. Management raised FY2027 organic revenue growth guidance to approximately 10.5% from approximately 10% and reaffirmed FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of approximately 16%, with margin expansion weighted to the second half. Flex launched in the U.S. in late June, Fit was filed with FDA ahead of plan for a summer 2027 launch, Vivera pivotal enrollment completed early, Flex received CE mark ahead of target, and the next-generation extended-wear sensor received IDE approval for an October pivotal start.

Dell reported Q2 FY27 record revenue of $47 billion, up 58% year over year, and record non-GAAP EPS of $7.04, up 203%. ISG revenue rose 89% to $31.8 billion with a 15% operating margin (up 620 bps), AI server revenue was $16.4 billion, and AI orders hit a record $60.9 billion with backlog at $95 billion. Management raised full-year guidance by $25 billion to $192 billion in revenue, with EPS of $25.50 (up ~150%), and guided Q3 revenue to $49 billion (up ~80%) with AI server revenue of $19 billion. Key change versus prior period: the company cited continued supply constraints (DRAM, NAND, CPUs) but expects a stronger second half, driven by AI and traditional infrastructure demand.

MongoDB reported Q2 FY2027 total revenue of $772M, up 30% YoY (vs 24% a year ago), with Atlas revenue up ~29% (fifth straight quarter near that level) and EA and other up 36% YoY; non-GAAP operating margin was 24% and non-GAAP EPS was $1.90. Net new customers hit a record 2,900, net ARR expansion rose to 122%, and RPO grew 91% YoY to $1.52B. Management raised full-year Atlas growth guidance to ~27% (up 300 bps) and EA/other full-year growth to ~11% (from mid-single digits), while Q3 total revenue guidance of $756-761M implies a sharp deceleration to 20-21% growth. The prior-quarter trend of accelerating total revenue and consistent Atlas growth continued, but the Q3 guide reflects a meaningful step-down that management framed as prudence.

BioLineRx reported Q2 2026 revenue of $0.3 million from APHEXDA royalties, flat versus Q2 2025, with a net loss of $4.3 million versus $3.9 million a year earlier and R&D rising to $2.9 million on GLIX1 spending. Cash and equivalents stood at $13.1 million, sufficient into the first half of 2027, supplemented by a $3.75 million registered direct offering announced the prior Friday. Management highlighted GLIX1 Phase I/IIa enrollment tracking to plan with the third cohort dosing in September and Phase I data expected in the first half of 2027, alongside new preclinical PARP-inhibitor synergy data, while giving no APHEXDA sales guidance and noting the Revolution Medicines pancreatic approval could alter the CheMo4METPANC landscape. No financial guidance was issued and no specific beat or raise was cited.

Lexin reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of CNY 3.19-3.2 billion with net profit of CNY 101 million, down 49.7% or about CNY 100 million quarter-over-quarter, on loan volume of CNY 55.43 billion (down 4.3% sequentially). Credit facilitation service income fell 43.6% to CNY 508 million and tech empowerment service income fell 14.4% to CNY 473 million, partly offset by installment e-commerce gross profit rising 58.7% to CNY 329 million with gross margin expanding from 9.4% to 14.1%. Management guided to a net loss in Q3, citing sharply lower loan originations, higher credit costs and one-time severance costs, and declined to provide specific full-year guidance; the board also changed the dividend policy from semi-annual to annual. Day-1 delinquency rose about 9.5% QoQ and 90+ day delinquency rose from 3.5% to 3.6%, with further increases expected in Q3.

Aesthetic treatment services revenue reached RMB 331.4 million, up ~130% YoY and exceeding the upper end of guidance for the fifth consecutive quarter (5% above the top end), lifting group revenue 33% YoY to a record ~RMB 510 million. Net loss attributable to So-Young narrowed 37% YoY to RMB 22.7 million, with clinic gross margin up 3.8pp YoY to 28.1% and 47 of 65 centers profitable. Q3 guidance of RMB 352-362 million implies ~91.7%-97.2% YoY growth, a sharp deceleration from Q2's ~130%, and the legacy information/reservation segment fell 35% YoY while other services dropped 48.2% YoY. Same-store sales growth accelerated to 52% from 14% a year earlier, and the loyalty program creates a 3-5pp deferral between service delivery and recognized revenue.

SAIC reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.9 billion, up ~5% organically, adjusted EBITDA of $193 million (10.3% margin) up modestly year-over-year ex a prior-year legal settlement, and adjusted EPS of $3.01, down year-over-year on the prior-period settlement offset by lower share count. Free cash flow was $131 million and net leverage fell to 3.0x. Management raised FY2027 guidance for revenue (midpoint $7.25 billion), EBITDA (10.3%-10.5% margin, +20 bps), and EPS, while noting a book-to-bill of 0.6 for the quarter (0.8 trailing twelve months) on procurement delays and an expected second-half margin step-down to the high 9% range. The company also quantified Project ORBIT at ~$150 million in annual run-rate savings by the end of a three-year implementation, with a path to ~11% margins in FY2030.

Frontline reported its best quarterly results ever, with Q2 2026 profit of $659.2 million ($2.96 per share) and adjusted profit of $580.2 million ($2.61 per share), up $235.3 million from Q1 on stronger TCE earnings. VLCC TCE averaged $152,700/day, Suezmax $111,400/day, and LR2/Aframax $92,400/day, with Q3 bookings so far at $156,900 (86% of VLCC days), $117,400 (79% of Suezmax days), and $81,000 (70% of LR2 days). Liquidity stands at $1.2 billion with no meaningful debt maturities until 2030 and a 52bp reduction in financing margins. Management described an exceptional tanker market driven by inefficiencies and inventory draws, but flagged the VLCC order book near 40% of the efficient fleet as a longer-term concern.

Q2 2026 group revenue rose 6% sequentially to RMB 3.4 billion, with net profit of RMB 427 million up 1% sequentially. Overseas revenue grew 18% YoY to RMB 930 million, and overseas operating profit rose 17% sequentially to RMB 154 million. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of RMB 11.5-12.9 billion but now expects to land in the lower half due to funding and credit tightening that began in July, with China loan volume down ~50% in July. Overseas volume is expected to grow double-digit YoY for 2026.

BW LPG reported Q2 2026 TCE income of $74,000 per available day, below the prior company guidance of $81,000 per day, with the shortfall attributed to negative IFRS 15 and FFA adjustments of $16.4M and $12M respectively. Profit after minority interest was $120M, or $0.79 per share, and the board declared a $0.95 dividend equal to 100% of shipping NPAT, exceeding the 75% minimum payout policy. For Q3 2026, the company guided to about $88,000 per day fixed for 92% of available days, well above its all-in cash breakeven of $24,900 per day, as Middle East disruptions, the Panama Canal drought, and longer Cape of Good Hope routes tighten effective vessel supply.

Chagee reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of RMB 3,415 million, up 2.5% year-over-year but down 3.7% sequentially, with total GMV of RMB 7,660 million down 3.3% sequentially and Greater China GMV down 4.5%. GAAP net income was RMB 465 million (13.6% margin, up from 2.3% a year ago), and non-GAAP net margin was 14.3%, flat sequentially but down from 18.9% a year ago. Margins and cost ratios improved sharply (non-GAAP G&A 9.1% vs 13.2% a year ago), while overseas GMV grew 114.3% year-over-year; same-store sales in July fell low single digits with August expected to turn positive. No formal financial guidance was given, but management cited same-store recovery and continued buybacks ($30 million of the $150 million program executed as of August 24).

BBVA Argentina reported Q2 2026 inflation-adjusted net income of ARS 131.6 billion, up 44.6% QoQ, lifting quarterly ROE to 12.2% from 8.3% in Q1. NIM net of monetary position loss improved to 14.7% from 14% and the efficiency ratio reached 45%. However, the NPL ratio rose 49 bps QoQ to 6.09% and cost of risk was 7.13%, though management guided to NPL stabilization around 5.5% and cost of risk of 6.5% for full-year 2026. Full-year guidance includes real loan growth of around 10%, deposits growing 5%–10%, an efficiency ratio below 45%, and a real ROE in the low teens, consistent with prior guidance.

Hafnia reported Q2 FY2026 net profit of $277.8 million, its strongest quarter since Q3 2022, versus $75.3 million a year ago, with TCE income of $372.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $287.3 million. The result included a $39.3 million gain on vessel disposals, bringing half-year net profit to $457.5 million, while net LTV fell to 13% from 20.2% and a $250 million dividend ($0.5003/share) was declared at the 90% payout ratio. Q3 guidance was framed through coverage: 80% of Q3 earning days booked at $30,716/day and 53% of H2 2026 days at $28,917/day, both below the exceptional Q2 spot rates of roughly $50,000/day but well above cash breakeven. Management described the market as easing but constructive into Q4, supported by inventory restocking (about 260 million OECD barrels by mid-2027), Red Sea and Hormuz disruption, and a clean fleet down 3% year-to-date, with CEO Mikael Skov handing over to Søren Steenberg Jensen on September 1 and no formal numerical guidance provided.

Jiayin Group reported Q2 FY2026 transaction volume of CNY 9.5 billion, down 74.4% year-over-year, and net revenue of CNY 636.9 million, down 50.9% year-over-year, swinging to a net loss of CNY 183.6 million from CNY 519.1 million net income a year ago, with basic and diluted net loss per share of CNY 0.89. The company suspended its dividend for the fiscal year and declined to issue Q3 guidance, citing industry-wide liquidity tightening and regulatory compliance effects. Non-GAAP loss from operations was CNY 225.7 million versus CNY 737.6 million income a year earlier, while cash and cash equivalents rose to CNY 504 million from CNY 43.4 million at the end of the prior quarter. The 90+ day delinquency rate was 2.21%, stable sequentially, and the 30-day collection rate improved quarter-over-quarter.

H1 revenue rose 22.4% to RMB 11.5 billion and China revenue grew 26.2% with mid-single-digit same-store growth, but overseas revenue grew only 15% against guided high-double-digit and distributor revenue fell 10%. H1 adjusted operating profit fell 6% YoY (up 5% ex-forex) and adjusted net profit fell 1.7%, with gross margin flat at 44.3% diluted by about 0.6pp of one-off U.S. tariff refunds. For H2 management guided group revenue to high single-digit growth (mid-double-digit full year), China mid-double-digit, overseas low single-digit, and TOP TOY flat; they plan to slow overseas store openings and take a net reduction of 50-70 overseas stores. Company repurchased RMB 520 million in H1, exceeding all of 2025's total, and declared no interim dividend, prioritizing buybacks at current valuation.

Nano Labs reported a first half 2026 net loss of RMB 316.7 million ($46.5 million), or RMB 13.65 per share, versus RMB 11.8 million (RMB 0.43 per share) a year earlier, driven by a RMB 250.5 million fair-value loss on cryptocurrencies from lower BNB prices. Revenue fell to RMB 2.8 million from RMB 8.3 million as iPollo V Series volumes dropped, producing a gross loss of RMB 5.8 million and an operating loss of RMB 291.7 million versus prior-year operating income of RMB 10.6 million. Operating expenses swung to RMB 285.8 million from prior-year operating income of RMB 21.3 million, with G&A up 29.5% and R&D up 39.8%. Cash stood at RMB 9.0 million at June 30, 2026; management outlined strategic AI/Web3 and digital-asset initiatives but gave no quantitative guidance for the second half.

Dollar General reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $11.3 billion, up 0.2% year-over-year (slight discrepancy with stated $10.7 billion prior year, but transcribed as such), with same-store sales up 3.5% and traffic up 2%. GAAP EPS of $2.48 came in ahead of expectations, including a $0.25 benefit from tariff refunds. The company raised its full-year guidance: net sales growth of 4%-4.3%, same-store sales growth of 2.5%-2.9%, and EPS of $7.80-$8.00, while also announcing a $700 million share repurchase program for the second half. Management expressed confidence in continued gross margin expansion and top-line momentum, though it noted persistent pressure on its core low-income customer from elevated fuel prices and inflation.

Q4 FY2026 revenue was $396.7M, up 5% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 29% to $255M (FY26) and adjusted EPS up 35% in the quarter. Animal Health legacy MFA grew 11% in Q4, while the acquired Zoetis MFA portfolio declined 11% on a tough comp. FY27 guidance calls for net sales of $1.55B-$1.6B and adjusted EBITDA of $258M-$268M, reflecting a prudent view on Brazil virginiamycin regulatory uncertainty; full-year adjusted EBITDA grew 39% to $255M.

Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR) reported a strong fiscal year 2026, with treasury-related income of approximately $553 million, primarily driven by unrealized gains on HYPE tokens and an effective token acquisition strategy. The company holds 29.3 million HYPE tokens valued at ~$1.9 billion plus ~$150 million in cash-like instruments, with no debt. Management highlighted a growing ecosystem, including new stablecoin revenue sharing (90% now to Hyperliquid), real-world asset trading volumes, and the upcoming permissionless prediction markets. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but management expressed a bullish long-term view on HYPE token value and the potential for continued NAV accretion.

Q1 FY2027 total revenue was $478M, up 15% YoY, and sales-led subscription revenue grew 18% to $399M. Non-GAAP operating margin was 16.2%, above guidance. CRPO grew 21% to $1.2B, and RPO grew 27% to $1.9B. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.998B-$2.010B and EPS to $3.29-$3.37, citing strong pipeline and consumption.

Autodesk reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $8.3 billion, up 16% as reported and 14% in constant currency, with billings up 10% and non-GAAP operating margin at 41%. The company raised full-year billings guidance to $8.575-$8.65 billion and revenue guidance to $8.295-$8.345 billion, including MaintainX contribution, reflecting outperformance and stronger second-half expectations. MaintainX is expected to contribute $60 million to second-half revenue and $70 million to billings.

Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 7.2% to $115.3 million, with DTC sales down on weaker traffic and summer trend underperformance; pre-tax income fell 24.1% to $11.6 million. Management cut full-year revenue guidance to $500-$525 million (from $530-$550 million) and pre-tax income to $60-$68 million (from $72-$78 million), citing traffic uncertainty, summer product miss, and the non-repeat of the Walmart program. Early Q3 momentum from the Halloween launch showed sequential improvement, but August comparisons remain challenging and performance is still below prior expectations.

Best Watch reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $9.8 billion, up 3.6% YoY, with enterprise comparable sales up 4.1%, versus guidance of ~1%. Adjusted operating income rate was 4.3%, up ~40 bps YoY, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.47 was up 15% YoY. The company raised its full-year guidance, now expecting comparable sales growth of 1.9%-3% and adjusted EPS of $6.70-$6.90. Management highlighted strength in computing, home theater, and emerging categories, while acknowledging memory-cost-driven price increases and a slower back half in computing.

Burlington Stores reported Q2 FY2026 total sales growth of 11% (matching prior year's 10% growth) and comp sales up 2% (at the midpoint of guidance) on top of a 5% comp increase last year. Excluding $55 million in tariff refunds and the resulting $0.64 EPS benefit, adjusted EPS grew 38% to $2.37, exceeding the $2.05-$2.20 guidance, while adjusted EBIT margin expanded 100 bps to 7%, above the 30-60 bps guidance. The company raised full-year EPS guidance to $11.77-$11.97 (up 16%-18%) and reiterated back-half sales guidance, planning to reinvest all tariff refunds into sharper customer values. Management expressed confidence in back-half opportunities but acknowledged consumer caution and weather risks, maintaining disciplined off-price execution.

Rubrik's Q2 FY2027 results exceeded guidance with subscription ARR of $1.66B, up 33% YoY, and net new subscription ARR of approximately $96M. Subscription revenue grew 37% to $407.2M, and total revenue was $427.3M, up 38%. Free cash flow reached $65.7M. The company raised its full-year outlook for subscription ARR to $1.88B-$1.885B, reflecting a 29% growth rate, and expects non-GAAP EPS of $0.47-$0.53. Management noted accelerating net new ARR growth and is investing in R&D and go-to-market for identity and agentic AI products.

Dollar Tree reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $4.9 billion, up 7% YoY, with comp sales growth of 3.7% (traffic +0.4%, ticket +3.3%). Adjusted EPS was $2.70, including a $1.31 net tariff refund benefit; underlying EPS was $1.39, ahead of the prior outlook of $1.00-$1.15. The company raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $7.70-$8.05 (from prior $6.70-$7.10) and initiated Q3 guidance of $0.80-$0.95, reflecting ~$0.50 headwind from reinvestments. Gross margin expanded 850 bps to 42.9%, largely on a one-time $383 million tariff refund. Management reiterated confidence in the long-term algorithm, with traffic turning positive a quarter early, but guided to gross margin pressure in Q4 on freight and inflation.

Gap Inc. reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $3.7 billion, down 2% YoY, with comparable sales down 1%. Adjusted EPS was $0.52 versus $0.57 last year. Gross margin expanded 20 bps to 41.4%, driven by Gap brand strength, but Old Navy comps fell 4% due to seasonal assortment and traffic issues, while Athleta comps declined 12%. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to 1%-1.5% growth, but adjusted operating margin outlook was raised to 7.4%-7.6% and adjusted EPS to $2.35-$2.45, up 10%-15% YoY.

HealthEquity Q2 FY2027 revenue grew 8% YoY to a record with service revenue up 6% to $124.4M, custodial revenue up 10% to $175.9M, and interchange up 5% to $50.4M. Adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 48%, up from 46% last year, with adjusted EBITDA of $167M up 11%. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.24. The company raised its FY2027 guidance for revenue, non-GAAP EPS, and adjusted EBITDA, citing strong first-half performance and AI-driven efficiency gains.

PagerDuty reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $124.4 million, up 1% YoY and above guidance, with non-GAAP operating margin of 24% and GAAP net income of $4.7 million. ARR crossed $500 million to $501 million, up $6 million sequentially, while DBNR improved to 98%. The company completed a 15% workforce restructuring and raised FY2027 revenue guidance at the low end, operating margin guidance to 25%-26%, and EPS to $1.33-$1.37. Management sees stabilization and improving retention but notes ongoing work needed.

IREN reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $137.2 million, including $70.5 million AI Cloud, down $7.6 million sequentially due to mining decommissioning. Net loss was $684 million, driven by $450.4 million impairments and $102.1 million fair value decrease on mining hardware. FY27 CapEx guidance of $25-30 billion with $4 billion ARR contracted by December 2026. Horizon 1 delivered to Microsoft, with Horizon 2-4 targeted for December quarter.

SentinelOne reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $292 million, up 21% year-over-year, exceeding guidance. ARR grew 22%, with record net new ARR of $56 million, up 4% year-over-year. Operating margin hit a record 10%, up 820 basis points year-over-year, and EPS of $0.08 doubled. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to $1.202-1.207 billion and operating income to $124-128 million, reflecting heightened confidence in demand, particularly in AI security products where ARR tripled year-over-year.

Q2 FY2026 net sales grew 8.9% to $3.0B, with comparable sales up 3.8%; diluted EPS rose 13.3% to $6.55. Gross margin was 39.1%, down 10 bps, while operating margin improved 10 bps to 12.5%. The company raised full-year guidance: net sales growth now 6.7%-7.2%, comps 3.2%-3.7%, EPS $28.70-$29.00, and increased buyback target to $1.8B. Management noted consumer resilience but cited macro uncertainty and elevated fuel costs as reasons for prudence in second-half guidance.

Workday reported Q2 FY2027 subscription revenue of $2.471B, up 14% YoY, and total revenue of $2.649B, up 13%. Non-GAAP operating margin was 31.1%, and cRPO grew 14.2% to $9.03B. AI-driven ARR reached ~$600M, up over 200% YoY, and AI products contributed more than $100M in new ACV, over 25% of the total. Management slightly raised FY2027 subscription revenue guidance to $9.94-$9.95B (13% growth) and increased non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 31%, while providing an early FY2028 target of ~11% subscription revenue growth and at least 200bps margin expansion.

Malibu Boats reported Q4 FY2026 net sales of $295.5 million, up 42.7% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $33.9 million, up 72.7% and margin expanding 200 bps to 11.5%. Legacy sales grew 13.2% to $234.3 million, driven by strong Cobalt and Saltwater unit growth. Full-year net sales of $914.6 million exceeded guidance top end by $29 million. For FY2027, the company guides net sales of $1.080-$1.120 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $101-$109 million, with Saxdor expected to grow mid-teens and legacy brands low to mid-single-digit.

Marvell reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $2.739 billion, up 37% year-over-year and 13% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.94 beating guidance by a penny. Data center revenue hit $2.17 billion, up 46% year-over-year. Management raised FY2027 revenue outlook to approximately $12 billion (45% growth, up from $11.5 billion prior) and FY2028 to approximately $18 billion (50% growth, up from $16.5 billion prior). The company expects Q3 FY2027 revenue of $3.15 billion at the midpoint (15% sequential growth), with data center growth exceeding 20% sequentially and roughly 75% year-over-year.

Harmony Gold reported record FY2026 results: revenue up 34% to ZAR 99.2 billion, net profit up 102% to ZAR 30 billion, and headline EPS up 87% to ZAR 43.63. Gold production was 1.43 million ounces at an AISC of ZAR 1.19 million/kg; copper production was 18,200 tons at C1 cost of $2.47/lb, both within guidance. FY2027 gold production guidance is 1.3-1.4 million ounces with AISC of ZAR 1.3-1.395 million/kg, and CSA copper guidance is 28,000-30,000 tons at C1 of $2.55-2.65/lb.

Lotus reported a 39% YoY increase in deliveries to 3,904 units and revenue of $268 million, up 23% YoY, despite ASPs down 3%. Gross margin expanded 160 bps to 10%, and operating loss narrowed 63% YoY to $95 million (or 26% lower to $195 million ex one-offs). Management provided a Focus 2030 roadmap targeting 30,000 annual sales and >20% gross margins by 2030, and highlighted strong early demand for the new Eletre X PHEV with 2,200 orders in China. However, European deliveries fell 17% YoY, and the company expects near-term consolidation of Lotus UK to widen group-level losses before synergies materialize.

CLINUVEL reported its 10th consecutive year of profit, with total revenue exceeding AUD 100 million for the second consecutive year, driven by a 6% increase in global SCENESSE treatments and a 13% rise in European volumes. Gross margin was 83% and net margin 36%, with cash reserves growing AUD 28 million to AUD 252 million despite an AUD 4 million FX translation loss. Management announced a planned Nasdaq listing and exit from the ASX, citing the U.S. as the largest future market and higher valuation multiples. Guidance for vitiligo phase III results (CUV105) and start of CUV107 remain on track for Q4, with total expenditure of AUD 53.5 million below the AUD 55 million five-year average target.

Titan reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $496.4 million, down from $546.4 million a year ago (same-store sales -6.2%), with a net loss of $9.2 million or $0.40 per share versus a $6.0 million loss or $0.26 per share last year. Consolidated gross margin expanded 150 bps to 18.6% and equipment margin rose 190 bps to 8.5%, while floor plan interest expense fell 30% to $8.1 million. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $17-$29 million and adjusted loss per share of $1.25-$1.75 were reaffirmed, but Europe revenue guidance was cut to down 30%-40%, with construction raised to +5%-10% and Australia raised to +15%-20%. Domestic ag remains guided down ~15%-20%, with a sharper second-half equipment sales decline (~20%) following earlier-than-anticipated factory shipments that pulled first-half deliveries forward.

Q2 FY2026: Group revenue grew 7% YoY to RMB 2.7B; non-GAAP operating income reached RMB 74M vs RMB 59M rebased a year ago (25% improvement). BEC revenue grew 5% with record Q2 non-GAAP operating income of RMB 107M; BBM revenue grew 22% with gross margin expansion to 56.1%. Management raised the 2028 non-GAAP operating profit target from RMB 550M to RMB 700M, citing AI-driven productivity gains and strong BBM momentum. Gap same-store sales grew in the 20s for the quarter; full-year BBM top-line growth expected at 20%-25%.

C3is reported Q2 2026 voyage revenues of $24.0 million, up 124% YoY, and net income of $10.0 million versus a $5.3 million loss in Q2 2025. Adjusted net income rose 755% to $9.8 million, and EBITDA reached $12.0 million. Fleet TCE increased 145% to $40,300, led by the Aframax at $133,500. Management expressed confidence that H2 will mirror H1, supported by fleet expansion and no Chinese-built vessels.

CMB.TECH reported a net profit of $364.4 million in Q2 FY2026 on revenue above $700 million and EBITDA of $552 million, including $127 million in asset-sale gains. The company declared a $0.64 per share distribution ($0.21 interim and $0.43 from share premium). Contract backlog was stable at $3.3 billion; cash flow for 2027 is forecast at $700 million to $1 billion after CapEx. The board maintained a cautious stance on tankers due to an order book over 30% on VLCCs and Suezmaxes, while dry bulk and offshore energy outlooks are positive.

Q2 2026 revenue of $1.2 billion was at the high end of guidance, with 3.1 GW modules and 3.3 GWh storage recognized; storage beat guidance. Gross margin of 13.9% was in line but down sequentially and YoY due to elevated freight costs and Jeffersonville ramp-up costs, leading to a net loss of $77 million ($1.40 per share). Q3 revenue guidance is $1.3-$1.5 billion with gross margin 13.5%-15.5%, and U.S. volume guidance for 2026 maintained at 6.5-7 GW modules and 4.5-5.5 GWh storage. Management expressed confidence in the new Section 232 policy as net positive for the company, and highlighted a 13 GW U.S. manufacturing backlog valued over $4.5 billion.

Gaotu reported Q2 2026 net revenues of nearly CNY 1.7 billion, up 20.2% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 66.5% from 65.8%. Adjusted net loss narrowed 37.6% to CNY 129.1 million, and operating cash flow rose 46.3% to CNY 861.2 million. The company guided Q3 2026 revenue to CNY 1,838-1,858 million, implying 16.4%-17.7% growth, a slowdown from Q2's 20.2%. Strong growth in non-academic tutoring (30%+ revenue growth) and offline business (high double-digit revenue growth in H1) was offset by still-negative operating profitability, though losses narrowed significantly.

Q2 FY2026 total revenue rose 8% YoY to RMB 7.9B, with gross margin up to 37.2% and adjusted net profit of RMB 704M, up 25% YoY, reaching an 8.9% margin. Advertising grew 28% YoY to RMB 3.1B, while games declined 14% YoY to RMB 1.4B. Management expects gaming revenue to resume YoY growth in Q4 and maintains a 40%-45% gross margin target, with AI CapEx on track at 70%-80% of the RMB 1B target for the first half.

In Q2 2026, Materialise reported EUR 70.1 million revenue, up 8% YoY, with Medical up 12% and Manufacturing up 7%, while Software declined 3%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 16% to EUR 9.6 million (13.7% margin), and adjusted EBIT increased to EUR 3.9 million (5.5% margin). The company reaffirmed its full-year revenue guidance of EUR 273-283 million and raised its adjusted EBIT guidance range to EUR 12-14 million from EUR 10-12 million, driven by strong execution and cost control.

CIBC reported adjusted Q3 FY2026 EPS of CAD 2.73, up 26% year-over-year (ninth consecutive double-digit growth), with revenues up 15% to CAD 8 billion and adjusted net income of CAD 2.6 billion. The CET1 ratio was 13.4% after watching back 7.5 million shares, and ROE rose 260 bps to 16.8%. Management expects adjusted expenses to rise quarter-over-quarter in Q4, with stable to gradually positive NIM, but noted trade uncertainty and no formal guidance raise.

Hormel Foods reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.37, up 6% YoY, with organic net sales down 2%. Adjusted operating margin improved 60 bps to 9%. The company raised and narrowed its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.45-$1.51 (from $1.43-$1.51) and tightened organic net sales growth to 1%-2% (from 1%-4%). Retail volumes declined due to portfolio shaping and consumer pressure, while Foodservice delivered its 12th consecutive quarter of organic growth.

RBC reported record earnings of CAD 6 billion, up 11% YoY, with diluted EPS of CAD 4.23 (adjusted CAD 4.28, up 11%). Revenue grew 9% YoY, with record revenues across most segments; adjusted operating leverage was 2.4% and the efficiency ratio was 52%. The bank reiterated full-year guidance, expecting positive all-bank operating leverage and mid-single-digit NII growth, while CET1 remains at 13.5%. Credit performance was stable but with a notable CAD 120 million incremental provision on a previously impaired utility borrower.

TD reported record Q3 FY2026 earnings of CAD 4.7 billion and EPS of CAD 2.77, with revenue up 8% YoY. ROE reached 16%, up 280 bps YoY, and CET1 ratio was 14.3%. Management expects total PCLs near the lower end of the prior 40-50 bps range, and reiterated a 13% CET1 target by H2 FY2027 with potential CAD 13 billion in buybacks in FY2027. U.S. Banking saw total loans positive sequentially, with bank card balances up 20% YoY.

Affirm reported its most profitable quarter ever, even without a tax allowance release, with strong growth across products including 41% growth in Pay in X and robust card adoption. The company guided to fiscal 2027 revenue less transaction costs above the midterm target at 4.16%, supported by solid funding costs and stable credit. Management emphasized network effects, expanding merchant adoption, and ongoing innovation in in-store and Affirm Edge, while noting consumer credit remains stable with no signs of stress.

Standard Nuclear reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.7 million, up from $0.6 million YoY, driven by first commercial fuel deliveries and service revenue. Gross margin was 67%, with net loss narrowing to $3.4 million from $7.7 million in Q1. Total contract backlog surged to $576.9 million (from $91.3 million at March 31) including funded backlog of $119.3 million after the Antares agreement, reflecting strong demand conversion. Management reiterated targeted Q4 2026 authorization for two new facilities and 2027 Richland production, but did not provide financial guidance.

Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue was $120.9 million, up 4.8% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.64 and adjusted EBITDA of $11.9 million. Full-year revenue was $439.7 million, up 1.2%, and backlog hit $367 million, up 14% year-over-year. FY2027 guidance was set at $455-$470 million revenue and $50-$55 million adjusted EBITDA, up from FY2026 levels. Gross margin declined due to component cost inflation, but management expects to offset this with price increases and see improvement in the second half of fiscal 2027.

CrowdStrike reported record Q2 FY2027 net new ARR of $333M, up 51% YoY and beating guidance by over $45M. Total revenue was $1.47B, up 26% YoY, with non-GAAP operating income of $372M (25% margin) and record free cash flow of $377M (26% of revenue). Management raised FY2027 net new ARR guidance by 630 basis points to ~34% YoY growth, citing sustained AI-driven demand and record pipeline.

Mesoblast reported FY2026 net revenue of $115 million from RYONCIL, its first full year post-launch, with Q4 revenue of $36 million and gross profit of $110 million. Net loss narrowed 44% to $57.5 million, cash burn halved in H2 to $13.4 million, and cash stood at $103 million. Management guided to double-digit RYONCIL revenue growth next year, with a phase III chronic low back pain trial readout in H2 2027 and an adult GVHD interim analysis expected in Q4 2027.

Q4 FY2026 revenue was $757M, above guidance of $725M-$745M, with non-GAAP operating margin of 26.2% versus guided 21%-23%. ARR grew 16% YoY to $2.549B, and FY2026 revenue grew 12% to $2.854B. For FY2027, the company guides revenue of $3.18B-$3.23B (12% YoY growth at midpoint), non-GAAP operating margin of 24%-25%, and free cash flow of $850M-$950M, while assuming continued supply chain constraints and increasing future start-date orders.

Q4 FY2026 sales were $151.8M, flat YoY and better than the guided down 3%-4%, with adjusted EPS of $2.06 unchanged YoY. Full-year revenue rose 2.5% to a record $579.4M, gross margin expanded 150 bps to 16.5%, and operating cash flow was $46.3M, ending with $108.2M cash and no debt. Fiscal 2027 guidance is cautious: North American production expected down ~2% and top-three customers down ~6%, with FX headwinds but partial offsets from pricing and cost actions. Management reiterated long-term gross margin target of 18%-20% and a new $40M buyback authorization.

Abercrombie & Fitch reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $1.27 billion, up 5% YoY, with operating margin of 19.9% and EPS of $4.17, beating its outlook. Results included a $100 million IEEPA tariff refund benefit; excluding this, EPS still beat guidance. The company raised full-year net sales growth to ~5% and EPS guidance to $13.10-$13.60 (including ~$2.10 refund benefit), and raised buyback plans to at least $500 million. Both Abercrombie and Hollister brands delivered record Q2 sales, with Abercrombie up 8% and Hollister up 2%, and APAC grew 19%.

Net sales declined 2.3% to $1.5B, ahead of the down 5%-3% guidance, with adjusted EPS of $0.62 exceeding the $0.20-$0.25 range, aided by $80M tariff refunds. Excluding refunds, adjusted EPS was $0.31, above the high end. Management narrowed FY net sales guidance to down 4%-2.5% and raised FY adjusted EPS to $2.60-$2.80. Digital returned to growth, up 3%, and Amazon sales more than tripled sequentially, though store traffic and body care remain pressured.

Salesforce reported record revenue and EPS, with CRPO up ~14% and free cash flow of $1.1 billion, up 81% year-over-year. Net new AOV growth was the strongest in four years, Agentforce ARR reached $1.5 billion, and AI/data ARR is approaching $4 billion. The company raised FY2027 revenue guidance by about $300 million in constant currency and announced a partnership with Anthropic to launch Claudeforce. Management expressed strong confidence in re-accelerating organic revenue in H2, backed by record pipeline and continued hiring of AEs.

NVIDIA reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $96 billion, more than doubling year-over-year, with data center revenue of $89 billion growing 18% sequentially. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.92, up 96% YoY. The company guided Q3 revenue to $108 billion ±2% and initial FY2028 revenue growth of approximately 70%, driven by strong demand but constrained by supply. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were both 75%, with guidance reset lower to 74% ±50bps in Q3 and 72%-73% in FY2028 due to memory price increases. Management announced expanded partnership with AWS (2 million GPUs through Q2 FY2029) and investments like $50 billion in frontier AI labs and $500 billion financing platforms.

Q2 FY2027 revenue was a record $2.01 billion, up 45.6% year-over-year and 16.7% organic; adjusted EBITDA was $315.5 million, up 53.5% and above guidance; adjusted EPS was $5.29, up 45.3% and above guidance. Communications organic growth was 16.7% but segment adjusted EBITDA margin fell 134 bps to 13.6% on investment costs, wireless deferral, and higher fuel costs. Building Systems revenue was $397.5 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 24.5%, and backlog hit a record $12.2 billion at 1.2x book-to-bill. Company raised full-year revenue outlook to $7.48-$7.66 billion, but is also deferring $150 million of wireless revenues into FY2028.

Kohl's reported Q2 FY2026 comp sales down 0.9% (improving from Q1's -1.0% and prior year's -5.1%), with net income of $151 million and EPS of $1.28, beating guidance. Gross margin expanded 305 bps, but excluding $150 million in tariff refunds, it was roughly flat. The company raised its full-year comp guidance to -1.5% to flat, and adjusted EPS to $1.80-$2.40, which includes a $0.65 tariff benefit. Management noted a challenging consumer environment and Sephora headwinds, but highlighted strength in proprietary brands, home, and kids, and announced a resumption of share repurchases.

Q2 FY2027 sales rose 4.9% to $169.8M, in line with prior momentum. Adjusted EPS climbed to $0.54 from $0.23, including a $0.11 benefit from IEEPA duty refunds; excluding refunds, gross margin expanded 340 bps to 57.5% on mix and pricing. Management discontinued annual guidance but expects mid-single-digit top-line growth and 55%-56% gross margin in the second half. The company maintained a strong balance sheet with $211.6M cash and no debt, and returned over $16M via dividends year-to-date.

Okta reported Q2 FY2027 revenue growth of 10% YoY and a record Q2 bookings quarter, with 30% of bookings from new products and over 600 customers with $1M+ ACV. Current RPO growth accelerated to 11-12% for Q3 guidance, and full-year revenue growth guidance was maintained at 10-11%, with non-GAAP operating margin of 26%. AI-related products, including Okta for AI Agents, are still small but contributed multiple million-dollar deals, and management expressed confidence in secular demand for identity security, especially with AI agent governance.

Ooma reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $83.2 million, up 25% YoY, with non-GAAP net income of $10.2 million and adjusted EBITDA of $12.4 million, up 58% and 74% respectively. AirDial services revenue grew 75% YoY, and business subscription and services revenue grew 38% YoY. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $332-$333.5 million and non-GAAP EPS to $1.35-$1.38, reflecting stronger AirDial momentum and positive residential growth from MyPhone.

Everpure Q2 FY2027 revenue rose 38% YoY to $1.186B, exceeding guidance; operating profit surged 77% to $230M with a 19.4% operating margin. Product revenue grew 54% to $687M, while subscription services revenue increased 20% to $499M; Evergreen//One TCV run rate surpassed $1B. The company raised full-year FY2027 revenue guidance to $5.0-5.7B (38% YoY growth at midpoint, up from prior ~25% YoY) and operating profit to $940-960M (50% growth at midpoint). Management cited a second top-5 hyperscaler design win for DirectFlash with revenue expected to materialize in FY2028, ongoing pricing power, and strong demand despite supply constraints.

Donaldson reported a record Q4 FY2026 with sales surpassing $1 billion for the first time (up 8% YoY), adjusted EPS of $1.15 (up 12%), and operating margin of 17.5% (up 110 bps). Fiscal 2027 guidance implies record sales over $4.1 billion (up 7.5% at midpoint), EPS of $4.22-$4.38 including $0.12 Facet dilution, and operating margin expansion of 90 bps to 16.9%. Management highlighted robust demand, improved operational efficiency, and growth across all segments, but noted continued pressure in power generation and industrial first-fit softness.

URBN delivered record Q2 FY2027 results with net sales up 10% to $1.7 billion and EPS up 9% to $1.72, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of record sales and profits. All retail brands posted positive comps, with Nuuly revenue up 29% to $179 million and operating income margin reaching 10% for the first time. Management guided Q3 total sales growth in the high single digits and reaffirmed full-year high single-digit sales growth, with gross margin expected to improve 25-50 bps in Q3. The company also highlighted a favorable tariff environment for the second half and continued strong consumer demand.

Lantronix reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $31.2 million, up 8% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.04, a 300% increase YoY. Embedded IoT solutions grew 34% YoY, and unmanned systems revenue reached $12.6 million for the fiscal year, above guidance. The company issued Q1 FY2027 guidance of $31-33 million revenue and $0.04-$0.06 non-GAAP EPS, and expects double-digit revenue growth for the full year. Net cash was $60 million, and the company closed the Nero acquisition for $11.7 million.

SFL reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $201 million (up from $174.5M Q1) and adjusted EBITDA of $130 million, up 20% QoQ. GAAP net income was $34 million ($0.25/share), with a declared dividend of $0.22/share, marking the 90th consecutive payout. The company added new car carrier charters and newbuilds, raising the charter backlog to $3.8 billion, and pointed to strong spot tanker earnings. Guidance was not formally issued, but management expressed confidence in continued cash flow visibility.

Synopsys reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.477 billion, up ~42% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $3.91 and operating margin of 41.6%, all exceeding guidance. EDA grew 8.5% YoY, design IP returned to growth (up 11% YoY), and Ansys contributed $711 million. The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $50 million to $9.69-$9.74 billion, non-GAAP EPS by $0.31 to $15.04-$15.10, and free cash flow guidance by $600 million to ~$2.6 billion. Management expects EDA growth to accelerate to double digits in Q4 and for the full year.

Photronics reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $216 million, up 3% year-over-year and sequentially, above the high end of guidance. IC revenue grew nearly 5% to $155 million, with high-end IC reaching a record 44% of IC revenue. GAAP EPS was $0.49, and non-GAAP EPS was $0.50. Operating cash flow was $76 million, and CapEx was $37 million. Management guided fiscal Q4 revenue between $207 million and $227 million, with operating margin of 19%-24% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.40-$0.56, while lowering fiscal 2026 CapEx guidance to $255-$305 million from $330 million due to timing.

Q2 FY2026 (calendar Q2) net revenues were $1.96 billion, up 6.7% YoY, with comparable brand revenue growth accelerating to 6.2% from 4.8% in Q1. All brands posted positive comps, including Pottery Barn up 5.1%, Williams Sonoma up 7.6%, West Elm up 6.4%, and B2B up 14.5%. Non-GAAP operating margin was 17.3% and non-GAAP EPS was $2.10, up 5% YoY, despite peak tariff pressure. Management raised full-year guidance: comp growth now 4%-6.5% (up from 2%-6%) and operating margin 17.8%-18.2% (up from prior range), with the raise driven by operational strength rather than IEEPA tariff refunds.

In Q2 FY2026, DSC revenue grew 3.7% YoY (14% QoQ), with adjusted net loss narrowing 61.5% to RMB 7.2 million from RMB 19.2 million (adjusted net loss was RMB 7.4 million per CFO, slight discrepancy). GAAP net loss was RMB 240.5 million including RMB 227.8 million IPO-related share-based compensation. Operating metrics: over 65,000 dealership MAU, near 200,000 user MAU, revenue from over 9,000 dealers, average revenue per dealer over RMB 6,600, 214,000 monetized transactions at RMB 259 per transaction. No guidance provided; management emphasized cautious, staged investment in AI and overseas expansion.

Q2 2026 net income was ARS 258 billion, up 12% YoY, with ROAE of 11.3% and ROAA of 2.1%. Banco Galicia net income rose 211% QoQ and 21% YoY on lower funding costs, improved financial instrument results, and lower provisions. Management guided to full-year ROE around 10-12%, loan growth of 10-15% (mostly dollar-denominated), bank NPL ratio improving to 6.3% by year-end, and bank cost of risk at 8.3% for the full year, from 9.3% currently. NPLs deteriorated to 8.3% in Q2 from 7.7% in Q1, but coverage improved to 92.8%.

In Q2 FY2026, the company reported total revenue of $219M, up 10% YoY, with Haidilao restaurant revenue up 4.6% to $198M. Operating profit surged 118.9% to $8.1M, with operating margin expanding 1.8 pp to 3.7%, but net profit swung to a loss of $1.93M due to a $4.34M FX loss versus a $16.33M gain last year. Customer visits rose 5.2% to 8.1M, and table turnover improved to 3.9 turns, but same-store sales fell 0.8%.
